* * *
I woke up early this morning to shoot some YouTube videos and do a hit on Newsmax. And predictably, the way it always does, the conversation devolved into the millionth argument I have been forced to have about Hasan Piker, the Twitch streamer Republicans are obsessed with and have decided to make the entire midterms about.
I finally had it. I looked straight into the camera and said that I understand they all believe the most troubling association in the Michigan Senate race is between Abdul El-Sayed and Hasan Piker. In reality, the most troubling association in that race is between Mike Rogers and Donald Trump.
As much as I have my own disagreements with Piker about some of the things he has said, he is not responsible for the state of this country and he is not the spokesperson for the Democratic Party.
They ended the segment before I could finish my thought, but Hasan Piker is not the reason you can't afford your groceries. Donald Trump is. Hasan Piker is not the reason gas prices are so high. Donald Trump is. Hasan Piker is not the reason you can't afford your rent or your mortgage. Donald Trump is. Hasan Piker is not stealing billions and billions of dollars from the American taxpayer. Donald Trump and his family are. Hasan Piker is not waging an illegal war and isolating the United States with a bunch of stupid tariffs. Donald Trump is.
* * *
#### _**[The reason the Trump administration keeps targeting independent creators like me is that we don't answer to a network or an advertiser -- we answer to you. That's what makes us harder to control. So do the three things that keep us in this fight: like this post, share it, and become a paid subscriber to Endless Urgency. Each one makes this movement harder to kill.](https://substack.com/redirect/9e2409ab-6e42-4341-b807-f613e2f7fed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

* * *
Everywhere I go on these right-wing shows, all they know how to do is talk about Hasan Piker or trans kids, and I am so tired of it. It's boring at this point, and it isn't working. The polls are spiraling out of control for Republicans. What they should be doing is finding a way to use the power they actually have. They control the House, the Senate, the White House, and the judiciary. They could use all of that to do something that might improve your life.
Hell, I thought Donald Trump's attempt to bribe the American people with a $5,000 check if Republicans won the midterms was crass and ridiculous. But if they really believed that was the right thing to do, they could just do it right now. Trump has the power to call everybody back. Mike Johnson has the House in recess because he is terrified Pete Hegseth is going to be impeached, and Trump could end that recess tomorrow. Mike Johnson works for Trump. John Thune works for Trump. All these Republicans work for Trump. That's the problem.
In Michigan in particular -- and I have done a ton of work in Michigan over my career -- people are hurting right now. Trump's tariffs are destroying the economy writ large. Everything is getting more expensive. People are frustrated, and they know exactly who to blame. They know it isn't some Twitch streamer they have never heard of and never watched. They know it's the President of the United States. The same man who promised in 2024 that the day he got elected, everything would be cheaper. That the day he got elected, the war in Ukraine would be over. That the day he got elected, the pointless foreign wars that exist to enrich a handful of defense contractors, oil companies, and corrupt politicians would end.
People know.
So they are going to talk about Hasan Piker to death and make him a household name, because they think he's scary and they think he's a communist. They're going to act with bravado, the way Dick Morris did when I debated him on Newsmax yesterday, insisting Republicans were going to pick up five Senate seats. That's ridiculous. I don't know what kind of drugs they're giving him in hospice care, but the man is crazy. And none of it is going to work. They have been calling all of us communists for decades. Would you like me to roll the endless footage of Fox News calling Barack Obama a communist, a jihadist, a terrorist sympathizer? I remember all of it.
They are going to tell you they're the party of small government. They are going to tell you they're the party of free markets and economic ideas. They don't have any ideas. They are a party of grievance, and that has been on full display for two years now.
The Republicans cannot govern. This is not simply about Donald Trump. Yes, Trump is the man at the top. Trump is the man driving the car and steering it off a cliff heading into the midterms. But these guys cannot govern. If they had any coherent ideas or ideology, they never would have allowed their party to be hijacked by a man so thoroughly unqualified to be president, a man who has surrounded himself with people like Pete Hegseth and Kash Patel and Todd Blanche and so many others who are just as unqualified as he is. They're carnival barkers masquerading as politicians. They're losers masquerading as winners. Yes, they stumbled ass backwards into an election victory in 2024, and I commend them for that. But they have done nothing to make this country better. They have done nothing to make this country stronger. And because of that, they have left their party with nothing to talk about but a fucking Twitch streamer.
As I told you the other day, the polls right now are out of control. Democrats are ahead in Kansas and Idaho (I don't believe that last one, but the poll said it.) They're tied in Florida. They're ahead in Texas. It's bananas. Maybe some of those voters come home, and we're probably going to lose some of those races. I get it. I know how the game is played. But my God, a lot of these races should not be close.
But the most troubling association in this election is between Donald Trump and the Republican Party. If they could ditch his ass, if they could admit the truth about how failed this president is, they probably wouldn't fare so badly in November. They can't do it, because they lack the moral clarity to do it. Their inability to separate themselves from an unpopular president who has a stranglehold on their base is embarrassing. It's going to hurt them electorally, and they deserve exactly what's coming to them.
Enjoy your Sunday. I love you all. See you tomorrow.

subject: Not a typical end-of-quarter email
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
September is a big end-of-quarter fundraising month for campaigns, so we’re guessing your inbox might be overflowing with panicky emails.
It’s sad how so many campaigns treat their supporters like ATMs — especially before FEC deadlines.
We are committed to treating you and other supporters with respect. That means we follow some (we think!) pretty basic rules:
* **YES** to sharing volunteer opportunities and emergency funds, supporting progressive candidates, providing informative content, petitions that go to someone that can actually act on them, and if you can afford to chip in, respectfully asking for your donation.
* **NO** to panicky subject lines, fear mongering, fake donor matches, clickbait petitions, or basically any tactic that makes you want to hit the “report spam” button.

We’re not going to beg, scare, or guilt-trip you into donating.
[ But we will politely ask: If you believe in a better future for working people, will you please consider donating to Alexandria’s campaign? With an average contribution of $17, every donation makes a difference.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260920.iJT4p8&refcode=em20260920-12321-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12321%2E2526796%2EbZbu0K)
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260920.iJT4p8&refcode=em20260920-12321-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=12321%2E2526796%2EbZbu0K)**
If today’s not the day for you to give, that’s completely okay, too. We’re glad you’re a part of this movement no matter what.
\- Team AOC

**[Donate](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260920.iJT4p8&refcode=em20260920-12321-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=1&akid=12321%2E2526796%2EbZbu0K)** | **[Merch](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/9251?utm_source=em-footer-20260920-12321-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=2&akid=12321%2E2526796%2EbZbu0K)**

Doug Burgum is building Trump’s Arch
Doug Burgum is building Trump’s Arch

| [|

| | | | Peter, **Interior Secretary Doug Burgum has announced that the administration is firing up the excavators to begin construction on a massive, 250-foot "Triumphal Arch" right at the entrance to Arlington National Cemetery.** They are ramming this gold-adorned monument to vanity forward without final planning approval, without required historic preservation reviews, and while actively ignoring a lawsuit from Vietnam War veterans who are begging them not to destroy the solemn sightlines of our nation's most hallowed ground. Burgum doesn't care. He took to social media to brag about the excavation, **proving once again that he views every sacred inch of American soil as nothing more than a personal playground for the elite.** [**Will you pitch in $25 today to our rapid-response war chest to help us expose Burgum’s corruption and hold the politicians enabling him accountable?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/IDE6FuFSakMuq1VcKe6qKA~~/AAUS1hA~/VzRGC1dbLrkD6nR5nb7w0s5ViLjtXcv8L4EtjSK74WyuS9Gy4vadowJUF02WJ4NFNV33RPHTMt0c7UnvIdwMD5pnSjGiNxXxEfOguK7BtUvw_swkgkW6DDkNPSTrfiVgvyzw-KUS4gB-8wTx0J1PF5FBj8C-xNlx1tFrajCFz3gN9K3q3rmVPvAlBg73gPQa3QV5BaXRfqzbXcP16yf1wuSU9-ei4VZq566To1pYO7fIsRpco0PEhE-HuPOH2TkV) We shouldn't be surprised by this un-American arrogance. The profound disrespect Doug Burgum is showing to our veterans and our national cemetery is the exact same disrespect he shows to our public lands every single day. This is the man who looked at the American public and declared that our wild spaces are simply "America's balance sheet"—**meant to be liquidated for mining, grazing, and timber.** He is the architect behind handing over prime, untouched federal land in the Crazy Mountains to his billionaire buddies at the ultra-exclusive Yellowstone Club, where he conveniently owns a $22 million condo. He is the one rubber-stamping backdoor deals to bulldoze gas-powered AI data centers into the Nevada desert, bypassing environmental reviews and locking out the public. To Doug Burgum, whether it is the hallowed ground of Arlington National Cemetery or the pristine backcountry of the American West, if it isn't making a billionaire richer or stroking a politician's ego, it is useless. At Public Land Warriors, we are funding a targeted, inescapable digital ad blitz to make sure every voter knows exactly how little respect these politicians have for our veterans, our wild spaces, and our laws. Friend of Life, It's easy to assume that God measures our lives the way the world does. After all, we're constantly surrounded by messages telling us to accomplish more, earn more, influence more, and become more. Success is usually measured by what people can see...In Scripture, we see something entirely different. Again and again, God reminds us that He is looking for faithfulness. When Jesus told the parable of the talents, He didn't praise the servant who had the most abilities or the greatest opportunities. He commended the servants who were faithful with what had been entrusted to them. That truth has encouraged us many times at PreBorn!. Most of us will never be famous. We may never write a book that reaches millions, preach to a packed stadium, or lead a large ministry. But every one of us has opportunities each day to be faithful. Opportunities to love our families well, to serve our churches, to encourage someone who's hurting, to share the hope of Christ, and to use the gifts God has given us for His glory. Those moments may seem ordinary, but Scripture reminds us that they are anything but ordinary. They are part of a life that echoes into eternity. That's why we've created a free devotional called _[Hearing Jesus Say, "Well Done."](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckE2OGyEQhU9D79rib_CwYBHJclaTTDbJEtFUuV0KDQjo8fWjTuILzLbe06ev3q83_xYoUV6_hQ3dWmr1rfu-x4i9U8_jcQ9jLUA9lfKbvOTSzNzOkvsQB32g12ECp4PRxpgJnTi_WiuFVC_T3XF708IaMKjMbYlCgLJaR5CAEayAidwB5FZyYSRX6iQWZV4AxA1Bv8bzwjRHoFHa6XBr2AkwDwrpFMs2JXcfo3amvjB5ZfLasJe9Reyn2nApLR8tJq8PTGmGknGuTF33sfl_PaYutZVeMQ7KK5PmiDYE2jemLrgFSv-PMWw10JqZuhywg_VMSh6YB1OXn8L_OM9fv7-_z8-vpuagPigl6ubMNF8P5F_18dmxP5z8EwAA__-w6ZJb)_ Over the course of ten days, you'll spend time in God's Word reflecting on what it means to live faithfully, steward your life well, and keep eternity in view. Each day includes Scripture, biblical teaching, guided prayer, and reflection questions to help you apply these truths to your own walk with Christ. Our prayer is that this devotional encourages you to keep following Jesus faithfully—one day, one decision, and one opportunity at a time. [**Click here to receive your free copy.**](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckE2OGyEQhU9D79rib_CwYBHJclaTTDbJEtFUuV0KDQjo8fWjTuILzLbe06ev3q83_xYoUV6_hQ3dWmr1rfu-x4i9U8_jcQ9jLUA9lfKbvOTSzNzOkvsQB32g12ECp4PRxpgJnTi_WiuFVC_T3XF708IaMKjMbYlCgLJaR5CAEayAidwB5FZyYSRX6iQWZV4AxA1Bv8bzwjRHoFHa6XBr2AkwDwrpFMs2JXcfo3amvjB5ZfLasJe9Reyn2nApLR8tJq8PTGmGknGuTF33sfl_PaYutZVeMQ7KK5PmiDYE2jemLrgFSv-PMWw10JqZuhywg_VMSh6YB1OXn8L_OM9fv7-_z8-vpuagPigl6ubMNF8P5F_18dmxP5z8EwAA__-w6ZJb) Thank you for allowing PreBorn! to encourage you in your faith. The Supreme Court has spoken: mail-in ballots will continue this cycle.
States can still count properly postmarked ballots that arrive after Election Day. The system is locked in.
_That reality changes the math._
**[When more voters cast ballots by mail, the advantage goes to the side that is organized enough to follow those ballots all the way home.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6172600/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfZWxjLXNjdG1pX2JyXzIwMjYwOTE4Lw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MjA/LbmNsZEFCdXZrWg/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM2Mjdfd3IyJmFtb3VudD0xMDA/garAIMA/s1r7bf2b82a)**

_That is exactly what ballot chasers do_...and the more of them we put in the field, the more voters we reach.
**Here’s how the scale works in practice:**

* One full-time chaser can build relationships with dozens of conservative voters in a precinct who rarely show up.

* Ten chasers can cover multiple neighborhoods and turn isolated contacts into early ballots.

* Fifty or a hundred chasers across key districts create a web of follow-ups that the other side simply cannot match door-for-door.

More people knocking, more flyers and information in the hands of unheard and underrepresented conservatives, more encouragement to vote early and return those ballots.
This midterm is not a normal election.
Control of Congress hangs on a handful of close races. The side that treats mail voting as an afterthought will lose those races. The side that treats it as the main battlefield has a real chance to win.
We still have time to build that capacity. But only if we move now.

I run a frozen pizza factory in New Hampshire. We regularly have trucks pulling up to our loading dock with supplies such as flour, cheese, pepperoni, and packaging. And almost every day, trucks pull away carrying finished pizzas headed for stores across the country. Those trucks don't run on gasoline. They run on diesel. And the average diesel price just hit [$6.43 a gallon](https://substack.com/redirect/ac335f68-8538-45c8-bee9-5cbad57531c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)...the highest price ever recorded in the United States.
That's not just a number I read in a headline. It's a number I see embedded on every invoice, every cost sheet, and every freight bill that crosses my desk. And that's probably true for most manufacturers. Inputs arrive by trucks run on diesel. Outputs depart by trucks running on diesel. And it's a number that is quietly raising the price of everything you buy.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/51cfaaf8-1ceb-4d23-9355-a4c8f163f1d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's run through the numbers. [Diesel averaged $3.69 per gallon in January 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/48667636-c6f9-44e0-8eff-2d471aff81ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Since then, it has nearly doubled and is up [58% year-over-year](https://substack.com/redirect/30b9c954-2c61-4787-9254-5d1601e1339c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Regular gasoline is [$4.47](https://substack.com/redirect/ac335f68-8538-45c8-bee9-5cbad57531c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); painful yes, but not unprecedented.
Why is diesel rising faster than gasoline? The simple answer is _chemistry_. Middle Eastern crude is [heavier than American shale oil](https://substack.com/redirect/30b9c954-2c61-4787-9254-5d1601e1339c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A barrel of Middle Eastern crude yields more diesel and jet fuel per barrel than a barrel of American oil does. So when the Iran War closes the Strait of Hormuz, [14 million barrels per day](https://substack.com/redirect/30b9c954-2c61-4787-9254-5d1601e1339c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of crude oil (roughly 14% of world supply) are disrupted. But the disruption on diesel is magnified. It gets disproportionately squeezed. American refiners using lighter crude can't address the diesel challenge because, well, the chemistry doesn't work.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5eeafcc4-112b-4d8c-9be9-6475cbcd8e54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And it's not just the Iran War that's disrupting the energy markets. [Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries](https://substack.com/redirect/5d90ec35-9e50-4776-b0fd-8ca98ca4a6c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have forced Moscow to ban diesel exports to protect its own domestic supply. Between the two wars, [refineries with about 5 million barrels per day of capacity have been shut down](https://substack.com/redirect/5d90ec35-9e50-4776-b0fd-8ca98ca4a6c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to Valero's chief operating officer. The world has [lost nearly 8% of its diesel supply](https://substack.com/redirect/5d90ec35-9e50-4776-b0fd-8ca98ca4a6c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with little spare refining capacity to make up the shortfall.
Gasoline prices are noticeable to most of us because we see them every time we fill up our car or drive past a gas station. _Diesel is not as visible._
But here's the key issue: gasoline is a consumer fuel; diesel an _economic_ one. That's because diesel powers **nearly every step of the supply chain**. Most manufacturing companies receive their raw materials and packaging via diesel powered vehicles. And almost every product on every shelf in every store got there on a diesel truck. Amazon packages. Building materials. And nearly every piece of farm equipment (tractors, combines, irrigation pumps) runs on diesel.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e2e2d984-fa2f-4be3-ab99-6de83e945e00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Diesel prices drive (pardon the pun) trucking costs, which means every product that moves by a truck is impacted. When diesel prices go up, the cost of moving products (which is embedded in the price of everything!) rises. And because farmers use diesel to power their operations, higher diesel prices mean higher farming costs, which will translate into food prices going up. A similar logic leads to higher construction costs and pushes housing up, too.
**Diesel may be the single most important commodity with respect to price levels, and it just hit an all-time high.** It's pushing your grocery bill up. It's pushing your rent up. It's even pushing up the price of your pizza. Everyone is watching the price of gasoline. But if you want to take the temperature of the economy, watch the price of diesel.

A few years ago, if you said an avowed socialist could be leading the Senate race in Texas, I'd have called you crazy. It's happening. James Talarico — the 36-year-old "minister" challenging conservative Ken Paxton — is currently leading by six points. Not in Massachusetts. Not in Vermont. _**In Texas**_. Talarico hasn't called himself a socialist radical. He doesn't have to. His own words do the work for him. He's said: ❌ Capitalism is an "oppressive system" and must be dismantled❌ The American flag is a "complicated" symbol
❌ White men are the greatest domestic terrorist threat in this country❌ God is "non-binary"
❌ The Bible is pro-abortion
❌ Christianity is "the most violent religion"
❌ There are six genders, not two That's not a caricature. That's the man in his own words. Strip away the "Christian" branding, and the policy agenda underneath is standard-issue far left: open borders, government-run healthcare, abortion up to birth, gun control, welfare for illegal immigrants, and a war on parental rights in schools.
And Texas isn't the only place this is happening. In Florida, DSA candidate Angie Nixon just won her primary by 12 points. In Oklahoma, DSA candidate N'Kiyla "Jasmine" Thomas won hers by 22. If either candidate wins in November, they'd be the first Democratic socialists ever elected to the U.S. Senate. And let's be honest. Socialist is their label meant to soften what they truly are **—** Marxists. **This rise of full-blown Communism isn't a fringe problem in blue states. Hormuz Traffic Just Quadrupled. The War Crimes Question Didn't Go Away.
A 10-day lull in strikes, a fourfold jump in Hormuz shipping, and a UN finding of 'reasonable grounds' for war crimes that the White House flatly rejected — this week's fuller picture is more complicated than any single headline.
|
---
Markets are closed today, so this edition reviews a set of developments that cut against the narrower, market-focused story this newsletter has tracked for three weeks. **Verified fact:** Iran has maintained a 10-day pause in ballistic missile and drone attacks on host states through September 19, with its last confirmed strike on September 8–9. Over the same window, Saudi Arabia moved roughly 2.8 million barrels a day through Hormuz across six days, compared with just 700,000 barrels a day in August, and announced pipeline restoration within days rather than the five-to-six-week estimate reported earlier in the week. Brent crude fell to $102.41 Friday, down 2.3% and a third straight losing session.
| | Regime Signal 01 — The Chokepoint Data Just Reversed Sharply
---|---
**Our interpretation:** a jump from 700,000 to 2.8 million barrels a day through Hormuz, combined with a much faster pipeline-repair timeline than reported days earlier, is a materially larger de-escalation signal than this newsletter's Friday coverage anticipated. **What remains unknown** is whether this reflects a genuine, durable restoration of shipping capacity, or a short window opened by the 10-day lull in attacks that could close again if hostilities resume.

| | Why the Distinction Matters
---|---
A president who disagrees with a policy decision while maintaining confidence in the decision-maker is a fundamentally more stable dynamic than one who attacks the decision-maker directly — even if the underlying policy dispute is identical in substance. **Next confirmation point:** whether this more measured personal tone holds through the weeks leading to the Fed's next meeting, or whether the underlying policy disagreement eventually produces a more personal escalation as it did repeatedly during the Powell era.

clean_body: What happens in the next 50 days will determine everything that comes after| | | | = A new Gallup survey found that 89% of Americans believe corruption is widespread in our government. That's up 10 points compared to last year. I think we all know the cause of that spike. Since taking office, Donald Trump has exploited the presidency in every way imaginable. The reported $2 billion he’s raked in since returning to office is likely just the tip of the iceberg. We’re talking crypto schemes, insider trading, private jets gifted from foreign governments, sweeping IRS immunity deals engineered by his own personal lawyer — the list just keeps going on, and the pace at which this President is abusing his power for his own personal gain is only speeding up. It’s no wonder another recent poll showed that the majority of Americans, regardless of political party, consider Trump both corrupt and dangerous. = The question is: what can we do about this? We know elected Republicans aren’t going to hold him accountable. They’ve made it clear that they’ll sit on their hands and turn the other cheek over and over again, pretending this is normal — and that in any case, there’s simply nothing they can do! That’s wrong.Congress isn’t a lesser branch of government answering to the White House. We are a co-equal branch, and it is our constitutional duty to serve as a check on the President. Flipping the House this November is about being able to make progress on the problems facing our country — from the insane prices intensifying our affordability crisis to the illegal and unnecessary war in Iran. And one big problem facing our country is our corrupt and reckless President. We need real subpoena power, real oversight, and the ability to demand answers from an administration that has spent two years trying to make itself untouchable. Because no one — not even Donald Trump — is above the law. The only way we’ll get that is by taking back a Democratic majority in November. =** If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If the corruption is so brazen that 89% of Americans can agree on this, we need everyone to stand up, demand better, and put real energy into fixing it. Fellow Conservative: As we race toward the midterm elections, there are two things Americans must know. **1) U.S. Senate races are _NATIONAL_ elections that impact ALL AMERICANS regardless of where you live.** **2) Electing strong _CONSERVATIVES_ is what matters, because another spineless Republican majority will not save our country.** Let's break these down... First, we often hear people say they don't really care about elections outside their home state. They can't vote for the candidates, so why bother? The reason is simple: _U.S. Senators make national policies that impact the lives of ALL Americans._ So while you may not be able to vote for them, their votes in Washington affect you and your family. **This is why conservatives in all 50 states must use their Constitutionally protected freedom of speech to influence the outcomes of Senate races around the country.** But if the entire Senate map is important to every American, which candidates matter most? The answer: _Conservatives_. Notice that it's not Republicans because many Republicans will not fight for our priorities when it matters. We've all painfully watched the current Senate Republican majority squander its mandate and fail to pass even the most popular policies like voter ID. Meanwhile, it has worked with the Democrats to spend so much that our national debt now exceeds $40 trillion. **The bottom line is that electing more moderate, pro-establishment Republicans is not worth our time and money.** That's why the Senate Conservatives Fund has selected eight conservative candidates across the nation who deserve our votes _AND_ our financial support.

body:
It's James Carville.
The primary is over. The match-up is set. And John Sununu and his Republican allies are watching Chris Pappas’s campaign right now — looking for any sign of weakness, any hesitation, any gap in resources they can exploit.
I’ve been around long enough to know what happens next: If they see it, they flood this state with money. If they don’t, they think twice.
_What they see in the next few days matters tremendously._
**[Rush a contribution to Chris Pappas right now. The general election has started, and we cannot afford to blink first.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260919_2.FNk08Y&refcode=em20260920-2&t=1&akid=9035%2E582294%2ENBPPES)**
Let me be plain about the stakes. There is no path to winning back the Senate majority without winning New Hampshire. **None.**
If Chris Pappas loses this seat, Democrats need to flip five seats instead of four. That math doesn’t work.
John Sununu has more than $30 million in Republican outside spending flooding into the state and more coming. He’s got the name, the money, and the GOP machine that has decided New Hampshire is their best shot at the Senate. They are not letting up for a single day.
Chris Pappas has won the toughest district in New Hampshire four damn times. He knows how to reach voters across the aisle and win. But he cannot — _cannot_ — go into the general election flat-footed on resources while Sununu’s allies are already flooding the airwaves.
So here’s what I need from you right now:
**[Rush a contribution to Chris Pappas today. $10, $25, whatever you can spare. Because the signal we send in the first few days of the general election tells the GOP everything they need to know about whether we’re ready for this fight.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260919_2.FNk08Y&refcode=em20260920-2&t=2&akid=9035%2E582294%2ENBPPES)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260919_2.FNk08Y&amount=5&refcode=em20260920-2&t=21&akid=9035%2E582294%2ENBPPES)**
I’ve seen races won and lost in moments exactly like this one. The campaigns that respond to the start of a general election with strength go on the offensive. The ones that hesitate get buried.
We are not hesitating.
**[Give what you can right now.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260919_2.FNk08Y&refcode=em20260920-2&t=22&akid=9035%2E582294%2ENBPPES)** Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.
— James Carville

We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3154%2E259176%2EK_wXdk) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3154%2E259176%2EK_wXdk)_

You may know me as the author of _Too Much and Never Enough,_ or as someone who has spent years sounding the alarm about my uncle, Donald. [**_I launched Transcend PAC to fund the candidates fighting Donald's corruption every day, who will strengthen the democracy my uncle is trying to destroy. If you can give, please split a donation between Transcend PAC and Blue Amp Action, and then read on to learn why I believe this moment calls for something transformational._**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16721?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.20_Mary-Trump-Uncle_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=5&akid=3154%2E259176%2EK_wXdk) | [BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR TODAY >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16721?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.20_Mary-Trump-Uncle_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=6&akid=3154%2E259176%2EK_wXdk)
---
**Here's what I need you to understand about my uncle: Donald is a weak man.**
That might seem like an odd thing to say about somebody who holds such a powerful position, but that's exactly the danger. Every day, as Donald deteriorates – psychologically, emotionally, and cognitively – he grows more desperate, increasing the risk to the rest of us.
Strong people do not rig the system in their favor. They don't silence critics. They don't seek to control the institutions designed to hold them accountable. **Donald does all of those things — because he has to, and he knows it. His behavior isn't evidence of strength – it's evidence of its absence.**
The comprehensiveness with which Donald and the complicit Republican Party are attempting to dismantle our institutions and take away our rights, in service to maintaining their hold on power and self-enrichment, should also make clear what is at stake.
Under Donald’s so-called leadership, the Republicans in Congress have stood by while our nation’s alliances have become strained; illegal wars have been started; and our institutions have been weakened and, in some cases, dismantled entirely.
I believe we are going to prevail. But when corrupt leaders like Donald and the sycophantic enablers in his inner circle go unchecked or unchallenged, they can do enormous damage. The antidote is to assemble a coalition of people who refuse to look away and are willing to take action.
**That’s why I launched Transcend PAC. Together, we’ll fund candidates who believe in public service and who will work to fulfill the promise of American democracy.** Because we deserve representatives who understand what’s at stake and are prepared to meet the moment.
[**_If you're able, please split a donation between Transcend PAC and Blue Amp Action today. Your contribution funds the organizing and the advocacy that will ensure no voice is silenced and all of our voices are heard. Every dollar will go toward undoing the damage my uncle and the Republican Party have done so we, together, can build something better._**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16721?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.20_Mary-Trump-Uncle_B4_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=7&akid=3154%2E259176%2EK_wXdk)

subject: People aren’t just ready for change, they’re hungry for it.
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-september-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260920_9237_fr&refcode2=9237_22930333_nL1EDH&akid=9237%2E22930333%2EnL1EDH)
---
Derek,
We have 44 days until the midterm elections, and in a moment, [**I’m going to ask you to chip in to the Democratic National Committee to help Democrats win up and down the ballot this November.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-september-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260920_9237_fr&refcode2=9237_22930333_nL1EDH&akid=9237%2E22930333%2EnL1EDH) But first, I’d like to personally share some things with you about what I’ve been seeing on the road.
I’ve traveled to some 35 states in the last year and a half, mainly talking with people in swing states and districts, and even so-called “red” states and districts.
Here’s what I’ve been hearing on the ground:
* **People aren’t just ready for change, they’re hungry for it.** And they’re hungry for a different kind of politics than what we’ve gotten used to — one where your blood pressure doesn’t spike every time you turn on the TV or log on to social media.
* **There’s a remarkable level of agreement among the American people on the biggest issues.** About 2 out of every 3 Americans agree on what the right thing to do is when it comes to health care, wages, affordability, tax fairness, and protecting programs like Social Security and Medicare.
* **The most important thing that Democrats can do right now is to persevere, even in the face of billions of dollars flowing through our political system.** We need to keep talking to as many people as possible, including those who don’t normally vote with us. And we need to remind ourselves that we are not powerless, despite what this administration and its donors would have you believe.

Derek, our moment of maximum leverage over politicians, over Washington, and over the people in charge right now is 44 days away. And when we come together to exert that leverage, things will start to get better — and not just better than they are right now, but better than they were before.
But that outcome is dependent on people like you, doing your part.
[**That’s why I’m asking you to donate to the DNC today: They’re doing their part every day by sending thousands of organizers to talk to voters across the country, by defending your right to vote in court, and by supporting thousands of Democrats running for office. Can I count on you to join them and do your part in these last 44 days?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-september-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260920_9237_fr&refcode2=9237_22930333_nL1EDH&akid=9237%2E22930333%2EnL1EDH)

Folks,
There's a lot of chatter from political pundits and election analysts about all of the things Democrats need to do to win big this November. It can be dizzying.
There's one thing they can all agree on: North Carolina is the most important Senate race this year. Winning here could mean flipping the Senate for Democrats.
I'm ready to win this fight to flip the U.S. Senate - and when I do, **we could have 51 votes to fight for the issues Republicans are ignoring and outright attacking.**
51 votes to expand health care - like I did as Governor of North Carolina - not strip it away to fund forever wars abroad.
51 votes to strengthen voting rights and protect our democracy.
51 votes to lower costs for working families, not cut taxes for billionaires.
I'm a lifelong North Carolinian, a former Sunday school teacher and two-term Governor who has always tried to put the folks I've served first. I know we can win this fight.
Republicans are coming after me with everything they've got - spending over $100 MILLION so far - and now a brand-now poll shows this race within the margin of error. I need your help today to surge ahead. **[Will you chip in $5 to help me flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://substack.com/redirect/9d8b5eb5-cd9e-49f3-a6e1-c8b6862432ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/9d8b5eb5-cd9e-49f3-a6e1-c8b6862432ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for everything.
Roy Cooper

clean_body: North Carolina is the most important Senate race this year. Winning here could mean flipping the Senate for Democrats. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Sep 20 | | | | | | | | | | | | Folks, There's a lot of chatter from political pundits and election analysts about all of the things Democrats need to do to win big this November. It can be dizzying. There's one thing they can all agree on: North Carolina is the most important Senate race this year. Winning here could mean flipping the Senate for Democrats. I'm ready to win this fight to flip the U.S. Senate - and when I do, we could have 51 votes to fight for the issues Republicans are ignoring and outright attacking. 51 votes to expand health care - like I did as Governor of North Carolina - not strip it away to fund forever wars abroad. 51 votes to strengthen voting rights and protect our democracy. 51 votes to lower costs for working families, not cut taxes for billionaires. I'm a lifelong North Carolinian, a former Sunday school teacher and two-term Governor who has always tried to put the folks I've served first. I know we can win this fight. Republicans are coming after me with everything they've got - spending over $100 MILLION so far - and now a brand-now poll shows this race within the margin of error. I need your help today to surge ahead. Thank you for everything. Roy Cooper | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Roy Cooper PO Box 1190, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

name: Roy Cooper
subject: What public service means to me
body:
There are too many people in Washington DC right now who want to be something
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1400&source=&t=1&akid=3602%2E124072%2EQHH1xn) | | | |
---
Here's what I think, Peter:
There are too many people in Washington DC right now who want to **be** something – and not enough who want to **do** something.
These elected officials and partisan hacks want to be the most powerful, the most well-connected, the most rich. Heck, my opponent in this Senate race, Republican Michael Whatley, has only ever wanted to be President Trump’s right-hand man.
Me? I don’t want to be any of these things. Never did. I just want to give North Carolinians the strongest fighter possible in the U.S. Senate and do what I can to make your life better.
That’s what public service means to me, and that’s why I’m running.
Candidly, this race is heating up: Super PACs are investing loads to defeat me, and polling shows this race statistically tied. **I don’t know what’s coming around the corner next, but I do know that I won’t be able to take it on without people like you by my side.**
[**_If you can spare $5 to my campaign today, we will put your donation to work immediately to help us flip this seat and take back the Senate for Democrats. You have my word._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1400&amount=5&t=8&akid=3602%2E124072%2EQHH1xn)

[**If you support my mission to improve life for hardworking families and flip this Senate seat, please chip in today.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139603623/647899955/-1037742479?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6138&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMzM1YTQzNS0xZmI1LWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ChrVjtbAY5e9K7cP6LSd173X-X2vjlqnucJUACklBtg=)

**It's insulting. It’s completely out of touch. And Ohio cannot afford Jon Husted any longer.**

Ohioans are fed up with my opponent's callousness and betrayal. That’s why we’re neck-and-neck in the polls. And with less than 50 days until Election Day, the momentum of our people-powered campaign has Republicans terrified.

| Peter,
Louisiana is MAGA's death star. It is the place where they test their most policies before firing them off at the rest of the country.

| | | | | | 🍂 September Update
September has been a busy month balancing legislative meetings, speaking engagements, and campaign activities across the district.
🤝 Supporting Second ChancesLast year, I was honored by Arouet as a "First Chance Champion." Since then, I have continued working with their leadership and supporters to ensure that women returning from the justice system have access to meaningful second chances and opportunities for success.I am encouraged by the growing number of corporations participating in the Second Chance Business Coalition, including major employers such as Waste Management, Mercy Care of Arizona, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Starbucks, Walmart, and Target.
🎓 Speaking with Arizona State University StudentsI recently had the privilege of speaking with students at Arizona State University during a LIBRE Initiative event. We discussed my background, what inspired me to run for public office, my passion for public policy, the importance of the First Amendment, and how citizens can effectively engage in the legislative process.
👮♀️ Honoring Outstanding Women in Law EnforcementFor the past two years, it has been a privilege to attend the Phoenix Police Foundation's annual "Women in Blue" Awards Ceremony.🏆 Commander Aimee Smith received the Elevating Women in Law Enforcement Award for her leadership and dedication within the Phoenix Police Department.🏆 Jessica Davis received the Service Behind the Badge Award for helping remove violent offenders from our streets and making our communities safer.🏆 Crystal Rowley received the Thelda Williams Up and Comer Award for her outstanding communication skills and commitment to officer safety.
🏫 Education Innovation Coming to ArizonaI was pleased to meet with a representative from the Chesterton Schools Network, winner of the prestigious 2025 Yass Prize and its $1 million award. Often called the "Pulitzer Prize of Education Innovation," the Yass Prize recognizes transformational efforts in education. Stay tuned, as this Catholic school network is exploring opportunities to expand into Arizona.
🏭 Touring Arizona ManufacturingOne of the highlights of serving as a legislator is touring businesses that are creating jobs and producing American-made products. Last week, I toured OMCO Solar, a leading manufacturer of solar trackers and fixed-tilt racking solutions. Their products are manufactured in Arizona using 100% U.S. steel and support projects across the country.
📺 Our First Campaign AdHave you seen our first campaign ad?▶️ Watch Here: [Campaign Ad](https://us.list-manage.com/_4TKZ4Lq1Zz?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)We've worked across party lines to:✅ Provide tax relief for Arizonans✅ Lower taxes for veterans and seniors✅ Eliminate the rental tax✅ Help secure our border✅ Make housing more affordable
📣 New Campaign Endorsements🏘️ Arizona Multihousing Association Political Action Committee (PAC)I am honored to receive the endorsement of the AMA PAC. Together, we are working to support safe, stable, and affordable housing options for Arizona families.
🏗️ YIMBY MaricopaI am also honored to receive the endorsement of YIMBY Maricopa. They support efforts to streamline permitting, reduce unnecessary barriers to housing development, and expand housing supply throughout Maricopa County. Arizona's housing supply is not keeping pace with demand, and we must continue pursuing practical solutions to improve affordability.

📰 Campaign Call to ActionDistrict 2 Residents: Want a yard sign? We'd be happy to deliver one. Simply send us an [email](mailto:info@BolickforArizona.com?subject=Yard%20Sign%20Request&body=)!Volunteer Opportunity: Interested in helping assemble campaign postcards? [Email](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I'd%20like%20to%20participate%20with%20Vote%20Bolick's%20postcard%20project&body=) our campaign team and we'll get you scheduled.
Thank you for your continued support. Together, we're building a stronger Arizona!
Best,Shawnna

I want him answering questions before Congress. = Blanche’s own Justice Department biography lists his work defending Trump. His new title does not erase that relationship —or the questions about how his department is handling the Epstein investigation. Americans deserve answers about the files. Survivors deserve transparency. And Congress has a responsibility to ask the questions the administration would rather avoid. Blanche should explain his department’s decisions in PUBLIC and answer directly about its independence from the White House. A former client should never get special protection from the nation’s top law enforcement official. As the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, I’m going to keep pressing for that accountability. The Attorney General works for the American people. He owes us answers. I need your help to keep that pressure on and keep fighting for a Justice Department that serves the public. = = Thank you for standing on the side of justice today. A building in Qamishli, northeast Syria, bearing the name Kurdistan. September 9, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair.
QAMISHLI, Syria--Faded photographs of the dead line the walls of Fadia Ismail's home in Hasake province, Syria--images of martyrs who died in the long quest for a Kurdish homeland.
Her son's image is among them. Dalil was killed fighting ISIS in the flat desert of Al-Omar oilfield in 2017 when he was just 29. Dalil "died for Rojava," she said in reference to the Kurdish-led political project in northeast Syria that gained de facto autonomy in 2012.
But now, as Syria's president pushes to integrate the Kurdish community of the northeast into a unified Syria, the dream of Rojava as a self-governing Kurdish state has all but come to an end.
"All of our martyrs have been betrayed. All the blood we shed and for what?" she raged. "What did Dalil die for?"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7da0adab-d447-42f0-a035-fbe025ed2a81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fadia Ismail sits in her home in Gerbawi, Hasakeh with her husband under framed photos of martyrs from her family. September 9, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair.
On August 25th, the Autonomous Administration of North East Syria (AANES), also known as Rojava, and its military component, the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), formally dissolved after more than a year of negotiations between the SDF and the new Syrian government led by Ahmed al-Sharaa. The talks ended when a surprise offensive by the government in January forced the SDF into accepting an integration agreement into a Syrian state. But many Kurds who spoke to Drop Site are fearful of rejoining a wider Syrian state that had previously marginalized and discriminated against them for decades under the Assad regime.
As the sun set on Gerbawi village in the countryside of Qamishli, Fadia and her husband enjoyed the cool twilight air on their porch. "There is no integration. This is the imposition of defeat," she said as she swatted at flies landing on the brim of her teacup. "Alongside Dalil, how many other lives were lost to capture Al-Omar oilfield? We lost it overnight."
"We have lost our chance at a better future."

## **Kurdish Women Fighters**
The SDF's fighters now serve under the new Syrian flag and the senior leadership are to be given roles within the Syrian government. Mazloum Abdi, the SDF's commander-in-chief, has been appointed as a special advisor to President Al-Sharaa.
However, their female counterpart, the Women's Protection Units (YPJ), who rose to prominence for their crucial role in the war against ISIS, are stuck in limbo, as Syria's Ministry of Defense has refused to admit women into its ranks. The YPJ grew to become one of Syria's most recognizable fighting forces, drawing global attention for its all female battalions that fought the Islamic State.
"Syrian law permits women to work in any position based on merit--except as combatants," Mustapha Abdi, a senior member of the presidential team for the implementation of the integration agreement, told Drop Site News. "There is to be no female combat element within the Syrian military."
The decision has left former YPJ fighters in limbo. In Hasake's Khabour military hospital, Isiyan, 19, was recovering from a recent surgery. In January, with the SDF in full retreat ahead of the government's offensive, Isiyan was ordered to get out of Raqqa, when her unit was ambushed on the road to Kobane. "I was hit by a Kalashnikov round that shattered the bones in my shoulder," she said. "I lost a lot of blood." She has been hospitalized since then, her days plagued by boredom and her nights by nightmares of what happened.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1ff6a067-683f-4373-9d3e-440bc8669b29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Isiyan, 19, recovers from a battle injury in a hospital in Hasakeh as her comrades visit her. September 7, 2026. Photo by: Anagha Subhash Nair.
Despite the attack, she is impatient to get back to her unit. "I miss my comrades," she said. Isolated in hospital, she seemed unaware of the SDF's dissolution. And like the rest of the YPJ, she had no sense of what her future would hold.
While integration into the Syrian military appears to be a red line for the government, Ruksan Mohammed, the YPJ spokesperson, said that, following the official dissolution of the SDF, YPJ leadership had met with officials from the Interior Ministry, and that "the possibility of integrating the YPJ as a special and organized force was emphasized."
"We discussed how women can play an important role in protection of rights and society," she told Drop Site. However, "no dates have yet been set for the upcoming meetings because we are waiting for a response from the Ministry of Interior."
Before the dissolution of the SDF, as integration progressed in all other dimensions, the YPJ had largely found itself frozen out of talks, and according to Mohammed, were only afforded a single meeting with the government in April.
Abdi confirmed this, saying that the lack of any further meetings was because the YPJ "were offered non-combat roles, such as administrative office based work, which they refused."
## **Violence Targeting Kurds**
The atmosphere is tense in northeast Syria following repeated incidents of violence targeting Kurds. Last Thursday, Sipan Hazni, a recently integrated Kurdish soldier was kidnapped and decapitated by Arab members of the Begara tribe. His killing set off the latest round of mass unrest, culminating in a riot and a fire at a prison in Kobane, which resulted in the deaths of seven detainees.
In Hasake city, the government's decision to end SDF-era fuel subsidies has left the city cloaked in darkness. "People can't afford the generator bills now, so they leave the lights off," Musa Kiki, 65, said. "What kind of government is this?"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/67195251-a458-4590-ba4c-2f1baf37391d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Internal security forces stand in Qamishli during a protest in northeast Syria. September 10, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair.
Kiki was attacked by the people who stole his home. He was part of the first convoy of Kurdish refugees returning to their homes in Serekaniye, a region from which he was displaced following Operation Peace Spring, an incursion by Turkey and the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army militia in 2019.
When he arrived back, he found his camera shop had been seized by a stranger and people were living in his house. "Honestly, I wish I had never tried to go back," he said, stubbing out a thin cigarette. "The house had been ransacked. There were no windows or doors. The stairs were destroyed and someone had ripped out all the cables."
"These people aren't even from the area," he added. "The person who took my home is from Deir Ez Zour, and my brother's home is occupied by an Iraqi, imagine that."
Despite the integration agreement stipulating the safe return of displaced peoples, under the protection of the Syrian government, Kiki and a number of other returnees were attacked by a group of armed men in the street.
"A large group of masked men came at us with clubs and knives, they were dragging people out of their cars," he recounted. "One smashed the windshield of our car and the glass injured my grandchild."
Ahmad Al-Hilali, the government-appointed deputy governor of Hasake, condemned the attacks, while Mahmoud Khalil Ali, the deputy head of Hasake's internal security forces, announced the arrest of several perpetrators.
However, the government's response did little to quell the simmering anger, with the attack setting off a night of rioting in Hasake province, during which protesters stormed Hasake city's internal security headquarters and burned the recently hoisted Syrian flag. The following day, a security point of recently integrated SDF fighters was attacked, killing one and injuring three.
Kiki has little trust in the government. Although the occupant in his home has assured him that he would leave once he has found an alternative place to stay, "there is no way to ensure that," he lamented. "If the government wanted they could go in and clear them out in a day, but they won't."
"Who can I complain to?" he added. "The government has done nothing for us."
## **Language and Kurdish Identity**
The issues at play also extend to governance and, in a crucial way, to language.
Behind blastproof walls and multiple layers of security checks, Jihan Said Hisam is busy in her new role as the newly appointed head of Qamishli municipality. Until June, she had been negotiating with the government on behalf of the AANES, until her name was suggested for the position during talks. Now, she sits in front of a large Syrian flag speaking on behalf of that same government.
"I am optimistic for the future," she said. "After 15 years of war, we can begin again and rebuild Syria." Before the interview, her press office informed Drop Site that she wouldn't be able to answer "political questions."
Not long after the meeting, last Thursday, a large column of hundreds of children and young men and women, chanting and holding placards calling for the protection of Kurdish language, wound its way to the gates of the municipality building. Young boys attempted to scale the blast walls, but were pulled down and scolded by the armed guards.
After a few minutes, to the whistles and cheers of the awaiting protesters, Hisam made her way into the crowd to make an impromptu speech. "Although we are having a difficult time with the government, I urge you not to stop studying," she railed. "Your education is vital and we still believe the government may reverse its decision."
"I stand with you completely and I will work to raise your voices with Damascus," she added.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49bc1b6a-8272-47df-a398-b43833900f81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jihan Said Hosam, head of the Qamishli municipality, speaks to protesters outside her office in northeast Syria. September 10, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair.
Despite the formal dissolution of the AANES, the office of the Department of Foreign Affairs remains a beehive of activity. In a plush office inside, Ilham Ahmed greeted a number of different officials.
Until recently, she had been the co-president of the AANES, but following the dissolution, Ahmed is to become a member of parliament with a role on the Constitutional Committee, responsible for overseeing the drafting of Syria's new constitution.
"We still don't know how much power the constitutional committee will have," she acknowledged. "Although we expect the parliament to play the standard legislative role in developing Syria's institutions."
While Ahmed spoke diplomatically, she admitted shortcomings in how negotiations are unfolding. "We feel that the issues aren't really being taken seriously," she explained. "Their approach is superficial and won't lead to meaningful solutions."
Despite that she recognized that the government has been willing to compromise on certain issues. "They initially offered us a deal which would have had Kurdish offered in school as an optional second language, akin to English," she said. "We rejected this offer outright."
"While we ultimately seek education in Kurdish, the outline of the integration file is yet to be finalized, so we remain optimistic," she added.
As part of the integration agreement, Kurdish--the language of education for the last decade in northeast Syria while it was relatively autonomous--is set to be taught for three hours a week, alongside an additional hour of geography, history, or philosophy class in Kurdish. This is designed as a transitional settlement during the next academic year while a final settlement is yet to be agreed upon.
Last Wednesday, hundreds of children gathered in the streets and schoolyards of Qamishli. They chanted in Kurdish, demanding constitutional recognition for their language, and rejecting Damascus's plans to return northeast Syria's education system to Arabic.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b4783761-2a6d-4f62-af9d-6c482fb077d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_ People protest in Qamishli against a decision as part of SDF-Damascus integration that reduces the use of Kurdish language in education. September 10, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair._
"I don't speak Arabic well. I won't be able to learn in it," said Jihan Hafer, 14. "If they make us learn in Arabic, then I won't come to school."
"I'm scared for my future, that I will lose my chance for an education."
Mustapha Abdi, a senior member of the government's negotiating team, acknowledged that the agreed settlement didn't go far enough. "To be honest, three classes a week is good in interior regions, but in Kurdish areas like northeast Syria, it is not enough completely," he admitted.
He explained that while 1,400 schools are set to teach Kurdish, the government hopes "the number can also increase in the next year."
"We have started now as a first step. We don't want to make the step too big, so that the step succeeds," he added.
Mezkil Hassan, a lecturer in Kurdish language at Rojava University, believes the policies are part of an effort to reverse a decade-long linguistic and cultural renewal that has taken place amongst northeast Syria's Kurdish population.
"The Kurdish people have learnt that their existence is connected to their language," explained Hassan. "This decision threatens the language and undermines Kurdish identity within Syria."
Rojava University, founded in 2016 as a Kurdish language university, and only recently recognized by the Syrian government as part of the integration agreement, is set to switch teaching over to Arabic according to Hassan.
The Ministry of Higher Education did not respond to a request for comment.
Many Kurds fear a return to the Assad era, in which "the state did not recognize Kurdish identity as a legitimate part of Syrian culture," explained Alexander McKeever, a researcher and author of the newsletter _This Week in Northern Syria_. "It viewed the Kurds as an alien population and so banned Kurdish-language instruction and cultural production."
The Syrian government has sought to allay these concerns. In January, Al-Sharaa issued a presidential decree that recognized Kurdish as a "national language," and annulled a controversial 1962 census that had effectively stripped citizenship from thousands of Kurds.
However, this decree doesn't make Kurdish an "official" language nor one that is constitutionally protected. In fact, Syria is yet to draft its constitution.
Despite the formal dissolution of the SDF, northeast Syria remains in a liminal state--not fully Syria, but not entirely separate either. The individuals manning the checkpoints are no different than before, although some now wear the uniform of the government. While the flag of Syria's government flies above public buildings, it is rare in the city streets, where the flags of Rojava and photos of martyrs remain ubiquitous.
The future of northeast Syria will not be determined by the change of flags or uniforms. After 15 years of governing themselves, those who sought to build an autonomous system are being asked to place their trust in a centralized state.
Whether that trust can be built will determine the success of integration and for the Kurdish community, it may come down to whether the new government can make them feel that there is still a place for them under Syria's new flag.

clean_body: Despite the formal dissolution of the SDF and the Kurdish-led autonomous zone, northeast Syria remains in a liminal state--not fully Syria, but not entirely separate, either. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Despite the formal dissolution of the SDF and the Kurdish-led autonomous zone, northeast Syria remains in a liminal state--not fully Syria, but not entirely separate, either. | | | Sep 20| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | Thank you again to all of our readers who donated to Huda Skaik, a Palestinian journalist from Gaza, as she begins a journey to university in London. We met our goal in just a few hours thanks to your enormous generosity. We're keeping the fundraiser open until Wednesday, and you can still give here: We also hope you'll consider supporting our ongoing Gaza Journalist Fund, launched last year to help 29 Palestinian journalists cover the costs of shelter, transportation, and basic needs. Please donate and share the campaign link: . | | ---|---|--- A building in Qamishli, northeast Syria, bearing the name Kurdistan. September 9, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair. QAMISHLI, Syria--Faded photographs of the dead line the walls of Fadia Ismail's home in Hasake province, Syria--images of martyrs who died in the long quest for a Kurdish homeland. Her son's image is among them. Dalil was killed fighting ISIS in the flat desert of Al-Omar oilfield in 2017 when he was just 29. Dalil "died for Rojava," she said in reference to the Kurdish-led political project in northeast Syria that gained de facto autonomy in 2012. But now, as Syria's president pushes to integrate the Kurdish community of the northeast into a unified Syria, the dream of Rojava as a self-governing Kurdish state has all but come to an end. "All of our martyrs have been betrayed. All the blood we shed and for what?" she raged. "What did Dalil die for?" | | ---|---|--- Fadia Ismail sits in her home in Gerbawi, Hasakeh with her husband under framed photos of martyrs from her family. September 9, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair. On August 25th, the Autonomous Administration of North East Syria (AANES), also known as Rojava, and its military component, the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), formally dissolved after more than a year of negotiations between the SDF and the new Syrian government led by Ahmed al-Sharaa. The talks ended when a surprise offensive by the government in January forced the SDF into accepting an integration agreement into a Syrian state. But many Kurds who spoke to Drop Site are fearful of rejoining a wider Syrian state that had previously marginalized and discriminated against them for decades under the Assad regime. As the sun set on Gerbawi village in the countryside of Qamishli, Fadia and her husband enjoyed the cool twilight air on their porch. "There is no integration. This is the imposition of defeat," she said as she swatted at flies landing on the brim of her teacup. "Alongside Dalil, how many other lives were lost to capture Al-Omar oilfield? We lost it overnight." "We have lost our chance at a better future." Subscribe to Drop Site or today. Kurdish Women Fighters The SDF's fighters now serve under the new Syrian flag and the senior leadership are to be given roles within the Syrian government. Mazloum Abdi, the SDF's commander-in-chief, has been appointed as a special advisor to President Al-Sharaa. However, their female counterpart, the Women's Protection Units (YPJ), who rose to prominence for their crucial role in the war against ISIS, are stuck in limbo, as Syria's Ministry of Defense has refused to admit women into its ranks. The YPJ grew to become one of Syria's most recognizable fighting forces, drawing global attention for its all female battalions that fought the Islamic State. "Syrian law permits women to work in any position based on merit--except as combatants," Mustapha Abdi, a senior member of the presidential team for the implementation of the integration agreement, told Drop Site News. "There is to be no female combat element within the Syrian military." The decision has left former YPJ fighters in limbo. In Hasake's Khabour military hospital, Isiyan, 19, was recovering from a recent surgery. In January, with the SDF in full retreat ahead of the government's offensive, Isiyan was ordered to get out of Raqqa, when her unit was ambushed on the road to Kobane. "I was hit by a Kalashnikov round that shattered the bones in my shoulder," she said. "I lost a lot of blood." She has been hospitalized since then, her days plagued by boredom and her nights by nightmares of what happened. | | ---|---|--- Isiyan, 19, recovers from a battle injury in a hospital in Hasakeh as her comrades visit her. September 7, 2026. Photo by: Anagha Subhash Nair. Despite the attack, she is impatient to get back to her unit. "I miss my comrades," she said. Isolated in hospital, she seemed unaware of the SDF's dissolution. And like the rest of the YPJ, she had no sense of what her future would hold. While integration into the Syrian military appears to be a red line for the government, Ruksan Mohammed, the YPJ spokesperson, said that, following the official dissolution of the SDF, YPJ leadership had met with officials from the Interior Ministry, and that "the possibility of integrating the YPJ as a special and organized force was emphasized." "We discussed how women can play an important role in protection of rights and society," she told Drop Site. However, "no dates have yet been set for the upcoming meetings because we are waiting for a response from the Ministry of Interior." Before the dissolution of the SDF, as integration progressed in all other dimensions, the YPJ had largely found itself frozen out of talks, and according to Mohammed, were only afforded a single meeting with the government in April. Abdi confirmed this, saying that the lack of any further meetings was because the YPJ "were offered non-combat roles, such as administrative office based work, which they refused." Violence Targeting Kurds The atmosphere is tense in northeast Syria following repeated incidents of violence targeting Kurds. Last Thursday, Sipan Hazni, a recently integrated Kurdish soldier was kidnapped and decapitated by Arab members of the Begara tribe. His killing set off the latest round of mass unrest, culminating in a riot and a fire at a prison in Kobane, which resulted in the deaths of seven detainees. In Hasake city, the government's decision to end SDF-era fuel subsidies has left the city cloaked in darkness. "People can't afford the generator bills now, so they leave the lights off," Musa Kiki, 65, said. "What kind of government is this?" | | ---|---|--- Internal security forces stand in Qamishli during a protest in northeast Syria. September 10, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair. Kiki was attacked by the people who stole his home. He was part of the first convoy of Kurdish refugees returning to their homes in Serekaniye, a region from which he was displaced following Operation Peace Spring, an incursion by Turkey and the Turkish-backed Syrian National Army militia in 2019. When he arrived back, he found his camera shop had been seized by a stranger and people were living in his house. "Honestly, I wish I had never tried to go back," he said, stubbing out a thin cigarette. "The house had been ransacked. There were no windows or doors. The stairs were destroyed and someone had ripped out all the cables." "These people aren't even from the area," he added. "The person who took my home is from Deir Ez Zour, and my brother's home is occupied by an Iraqi, imagine that." Despite the integration agreement stipulating the safe return of displaced peoples, under the protection of the Syrian government, Kiki and a number of other returnees were attacked by a group of armed men in the street. "A large group of masked men came at us with clubs and knives, they were dragging people out of their cars," he recounted. "One smashed the windshield of our car and the glass injured my grandchild." Ahmad Al-Hilali, the government-appointed deputy governor of Hasake, condemned the attacks, while Mahmoud Khalil Ali, the deputy head of Hasake's internal security forces, announced the arrest of several perpetrators. However, the government's response did little to quell the simmering anger, with the attack setting off a night of rioting in Hasake province, during which protesters stormed Hasake city's internal security headquarters and burned the recently hoisted Syrian flag. The following day, a security point of recently integrated SDF fighters was attacked, killing one and injuring three. Kiki has little trust in the government. Although the occupant in his home has assured him that he would leave once he has found an alternative place to stay, "there is no way to ensure that," he lamented. "If the government wanted they could go in and clear them out in a day, but they won't." "Who can I complain to?" he added. "The government has done nothing for us." Language and Kurdish Identity The issues at play also extend to governance and, in a crucial way, to language. Behind blastproof walls and multiple layers of security checks, Jihan Said Hisam is busy in her new role as the newly appointed head of Qamishli municipality. Until June, she had been negotiating with the government on behalf of the AANES, until her name was suggested for the position during talks. Now, she sits in front of a large Syrian flag speaking on behalf of that same government. "I am optimistic for the future," she said. "After 15 years of war, we can begin again and rebuild Syria." Before the interview, her press office informed Drop Site that she wouldn't be able to answer "political questions." Not long after the meeting, last Thursday, a large column of hundreds of children and young men and women, chanting and holding placards calling for the protection of Kurdish language, wound its way to the gates of the municipality building. Young boys attempted to scale the blast walls, but were pulled down and scolded by the armed guards. After a few minutes, to the whistles and cheers of the awaiting protesters, Hisam made her way into the crowd to make an impromptu speech. "Although we are having a difficult time with the government, I urge you not to stop studying," she railed. "Your education is vital and we still believe the government may reverse its decision." "I stand with you completely and I will work to raise your voices with Damascus," she added. | | ---|---|--- Jihan Said Hosam, head of the Qamishli municipality, speaks to protesters outside her office in northeast Syria. September 10, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair. Despite the formal dissolution of the AANES, the office of the Department of Foreign Affairs remains a beehive of activity. In a plush office inside, Ilham Ahmed greeted a number of different officials. Until recently, she had been the co-president of the AANES, but following the dissolution, Ahmed is to become a member of parliament with a role on the Constitutional Committee, responsible for overseeing the drafting of Syria's new constitution. "We still don't know how much power the constitutional committee will have," she acknowledged. "Although we expect the parliament to play the standard legislative role in developing Syria's institutions." While Ahmed spoke diplomatically, she admitted shortcomings in how negotiations are unfolding. "We feel that the issues aren't really being taken seriously," she explained. "Their approach is superficial and won't lead to meaningful solutions." Despite that she recognized that the government has been willing to compromise on certain issues. "They initially offered us a deal which would have had Kurdish offered in school as an optional second language, akin to English," she said. "We rejected this offer outright." "While we ultimately seek education in Kurdish, the outline of the integration file is yet to be finalized, so we remain optimistic," she added. As part of the integration agreement, Kurdish--the language of education for the last decade in northeast Syria while it was relatively autonomous--is set to be taught for three hours a week, alongside an additional hour of geography, history, or philosophy class in Kurdish. This is designed as a transitional settlement during the next academic year while a final settlement is yet to be agreed upon. Last Wednesday, hundreds of children gathered in the streets and schoolyards of Qamishli. They chanted in Kurdish, demanding constitutional recognition for their language, and rejecting Damascus's plans to return northeast Syria's education system to Arabic. | | ---|---|--- People protest in Qamishli against a decision as part of SDF-Damascus integration that reduces the use of Kurdish language in education. September 10, 2026. Photo by Anagha Subhash Nair. "I don't speak Arabic well. I won't be able to learn in it," said Jihan Hafer, 14. "If they make us learn in Arabic, then I won't come to school." "I'm scared for my future, that I will lose my chance for an education." Mustapha Abdi, a senior member of the government's negotiating team, acknowledged that the agreed settlement didn't go far enough. "To be honest, three classes a week is good in interior regions, but in Kurdish areas like northeast Syria, it is not enough completely," he admitted. He explained that while 1,400 schools are set to teach Kurdish, the government hopes "the number can also increase in the next year." "We have started now as a first step. We don't want to make the step too big, so that the step succeeds," he added. Mezkil Hassan, a lecturer in Kurdish language at Rojava University, believes the policies are part of an effort to reverse a decade-long linguistic and cultural renewal that has taken place amongst northeast Syria's Kurdish population. "The Kurdish people have learnt that their existence is connected to their language," explained Hassan. "This decision threatens the language and undermines Kurdish identity within Syria." Rojava University, founded in 2016 as a Kurdish language university, and only recently recognized by the Syrian government as part of the integration agreement, is set to switch teaching over to Arabic according to Hassan. The Ministry of Higher Education did not respond to a request for comment. Many Kurds fear a return to the Assad era, in which "the state did not recognize Kurdish identity as a legitimate part of Syrian culture," explained Alexander McKeever, a researcher and author of the newsletter This Week in Northern Syria. "It viewed the Kurds as an alien population and so banned Kurdish-language instruction and cultural production." The Syrian government has sought to allay these concerns. In January, Al-Sharaa issued a presidential decree that recognized Kurdish as a "national language," and annulled a controversial 1962 census that had effectively stripped citizenship from thousands of Kurds. However, this decree doesn't make Kurdish an "official" language nor one that is constitutionally protected. In fact, Syria is yet to draft its constitution. Despite the formal dissolution of the SDF, northeast Syria remains in a liminal state--not fully Syria, but not entirely separate either. The individuals manning the checkpoints are no different than before, although some now wear the uniform of the government. While the flag of Syria's government flies above public buildings, it is rare in the city streets, where the flags of Rojava and photos of martyrs remain ubiquitous. The future of northeast Syria will not be determined by the change of flags or uniforms. After 15 years of governing themselves, those who sought to build an autonomous system are being asked to place their trust in a centralized state. Whether that trust can be built will determine the success of integration and for the Kurdish community, it may come down to whether the new government can make them feel that there is still a place for them under Syria's new flag. | A guest post by| journalist based in Damascus Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. * Ban members of Congress and their staff from placing insider bets on prediction markets.
* Ban members of Congress from becoming lobbyists after they leave office and getting rich off the industries they were _supposed_ to regulate.
* Mandatory prison time for elected officials if caught stealing taxpayer dollars.

The bottom line is: there are real ways to clean up politics and restore accountability — and I’m ready to make them. But first, I could really use your help.
