| | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0EtupDAQBuDTmB3IDx7NwouRELseaUajydIq7AKs2MayTff1I5L0BbKt_9enqnq7qztYZ8P2GzzKVFaVslrBln09XcCcbX7uUDyUgikrTnlf07HmVIEu9oGqhcpIow0wXaFkw20cBe9ZV-1y5TCYTnPNejYs7a0D0wkuxt4YAwvDysrLoyOnbBSU8QaHpVspBUMN8pYCaSk4TKVJGM_FWQ2hQH5fj6Sx0YevnNxLiZmIX4TPhM8J83EmjbmJCZcjhatF-PxE52pzBKwjEfNZvPrqETHFdOSIutiwEd5fkUdjT0_EhB6s-x5q8BHsFoiYLuyyXskRCoZCxPSfqT9D_fffXL_uqpI08Wmds7kfSEu3S_zcvPzw2Q_JPwIAAP__KVuSyA)
---
Friend of Life, It's easy to assume that God measures our lives the way the world does. After all, we're constantly surrounded by messages telling us to accomplish more, earn more, influence more, and become more. Success is usually measured by what people can see...In Scripture, we see something entirely different. Again and again, God reminds us that He is looking for faithfulness. When Jesus told the parable of the talents, He didn't praise the servant who had the most abilities or the greatest opportunities. He commended the servants who were faithful with what had been entrusted to them. That truth has encouraged us many times at PreBorn!. Most of us will never be famous. We may never write a book that reaches millions, preach to a packed stadium, or lead a large ministry. But every one of us has opportunities each day to be faithful. Opportunities to love our families well, to serve our churches, to encourage someone who's hurting, to share the hope of Christ, and to use the gifts God has given us for His glory. Those moments may seem ordinary, but Scripture reminds us that they are anything but ordinary. They are part of a life that echoes into eternity. That's why we've created a free devotional called _[Hearing Jesus Say, "Well Done."](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0EtupDAQBuDTmB3IDx7NwouRELseaUajydIq7AKs2MayTff1I5L0BbKt_9enqnq7qztYZ8P2GzzKVFaVslrBln09XcCcbX7uUDyUgikrTnlf07HmVIEu9oGqhcpIow0wXaFkw20cBe9ZV-1y5TCYTnPNejYs7a0D0wkuxt4YAwvDysrLoyOnbBSU8QaHpVspBUMN8pYCaSk4TKVJGM_FWQ2hQH5fj6Sx0YevnNxLiZmIX4TPhM8J83EmjbmJCZcjhatF-PxE52pzBKwjEfNZvPrqETHFdOSIutiwEd5fkUdjT0_EhB6s-x5q8BHsFoiYLuyyXskRCoZCxPSfqT9D_fffXL_uqpI08Wmds7kfSEu3S_zcvPzw2Q_JPwIAAP__KVuSyA)_ Over the course of ten days, you'll spend time in God's Word reflecting on what it means to live faithfully, steward your life well, and keep eternity in view. Each day includes Scripture, biblical teaching, guided prayer, and reflection questions to help you apply these truths to your own walk with Christ. Our prayer is that this devotional encourages you to keep following Jesus faithfully—one day, one decision, and one opportunity at a time. Peter,
I want to share something that means a great deal to me.
The Blue Dog PAC just endorsed this campaign. And for a Tennessean, that carries real weight.
Former Tennessee Congressman John Tanner of Union City was among the founders of the Blue Dog Coalition. Former Congressmen Jim Cooper, Bart Gordon, Lincoln Davis, and Harold Ford Jr. carried that tradition forward in Congress, representing Tennessee. They represented different corners of our state and different generations of Tennesseans, but they shared something in common: they never forgot who sent them there.

Peter,
I will work with anybody. **_But I will bow to nobody._**
I didn’t come from money or prestige. As the son of an immigrant single mother, I came from hard work, community, and an unshakeable belief that _we could do better._
**[If you share that belief, would you chip in $5 to our re-election campaign today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260920-2.917GRc&refcode=em-20260920-2&t=2&akid=1959%2E1086043%2EYbn6--)**
Peter, my grandfather was run out of his home by the Klan. **But he rebuilt anyway.**
That history and resilience is why I believe every family deserves a fair shot at work, wages, and wealth — not just survival.
That’s what we’re building together: Teacher vacancies cut in half. Violent crime at historic lows. The first statewide Service Year Option in the country for every high school graduate.
My MAGA Republican opponent would undo all of it. **And I will not bow to him, or anyone who wants to take Maryland backward.**

| | | Hi, it’s Darren Soto. I just won the official Democratic nomination to represent FL-09 in Congress. My campaign is centered on the 3 C’s: Lower costs. Protect our care. Stop corruption.

But accomplishing those goals depends on who controls the House.

Here are five reasons I’m asking you to contribute $5:

**1\. Lower grocery, fuel, and housing costs.** Congress must challenge tariffs and other policies that increase prices for Central Florida families and farmers.

**2\. Protect Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act.** Families should not lose coverage or face dramatically higher premiums because of a vote in Washington.

**3\. Defend Social Security and Medicare.** Central Florida seniors earned these benefits, and we must protect them.

**4\. Continue investing in our growing region.** Infrastructure, transportation, disaster preparedness, and high-paying technology jobs require effective federal partnerships.

**5\. Protect FL-09 and change the House majority.** Our district has been dramatically redrawn, making the resources needed to communicate with new voters more important than ever.

This is disgusting and outrageous:

Donald Trump just announced that he will allow _over 300,000 metric tons_ of ground beef to be imported on a fast-track and with none of the regular tariffs he slapped on other imports.

Trump said that he “didn’t want to say” from where the beef would originate. Others in his Administration hinted at concerns about **diseases** among cattle herds in Argentina, a right-wing ally of Trump and the country where most of the ground beef likely will come from.

Clueless Agriculture Secretary, MAGA donor Brooke Rollins, admitted in a live interview that she had _no idea_ where the beef is going to come from and that she was “not part of those conversations”:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Friends,
I've been sharing a lot of stories about our campaign lately: former Republican Gov. Bill Graves' endorsement, my debate against Roger Marshall at the Kansas State Fair and even my visit to Dorothy's House and the Land of Oz in Liberal, Kansas. But today, I want to pull back the curtain and give you a behind-the-scenes look at one of the most important moments of my campaign: the final FEC end-of-quarter deadline coming up on Sept. 30.
I'll be honest: before I stepped up to run for the U.S. Senate, I didn't understand what all the FEC fuss was about. But now, I know that these deadlines can make or break a campaign. That's why I wanted to talk to you about them today.
You see, when someone wants to run for office at the federal level, they're required to file with the Federal Election Commission. At the end of each quarter, each campaign is required by law to report their fundraising numbers to the agency.
Anyone can read those reports -- and they do. Everyone from the media to the candidate's supporters and opponents look at the fundraising numbers to try and answer that all-important question: _Does the campaign have the strength and support they need to win?_
**That brings us to** _**this**_**crucial moment, friend.**
With our final FEC end-of-quarter deadline of this race just ten days away, time is running out.
Roger Marshall's allies know that a recent poll shows us with a 2-point lead. Now, they'll be watching to see if our fundraising can back that up. If it doesn't, they'll think we're vulnerable -- and increase their spending and attack ads accordingly.
But that's not the only reason this deadline is so important. When we launched this campaign, our fundraising numbers went through the roof. Same when we won the primary. That momentum was a clear indication that voters in Kansas, and throughout the country, resonated with our unifying message. The fundraising success we had played a pivotal role in drawing national attention to this race, not to mention helping us launch ads and meet with hundreds of Kansans. And _that_ is why we're up by two points with a historic opportunity to flip this seat.
Now, with Election Day and this final FEC quarterly deadline fast approaching, we have to prove those early successes weren't flukes.
**That 's what makes this so important. We only have until midnight on Sept. 30 to show **_**everyone**_**that our momentum is still going strong and our grassroots movement has what it takes to win.**
This is one of our last chances to show Marshall and his allies that Kansas is ready for real leadership. It's our final opportunity to make sure everyone in our great state -- and throughout this country -- knows that I will stand up for them against the corrupt politicians in Washington.
But unlike Roger Marshall, I refuse to accept corporate PAC money. That's why I'm counting on grassroots supporters like you to help make sure we finish out the quarter strong.
**[Every dollar gets us closer to bringing real change and progress to the Senate. Please, will you make a donation today to show Roger Marshall and his dark-money allies that our movement is unstoppable?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/de3d231c-ee8b-4f15-b462-af96063db040?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/de3d231c-ee8b-4f15-b462-af96063db040?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**This is it, folks. It 's go time.**
Thank you for standing with me,
Adam Hamilton

subject: This election isn’t about me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
I’m honored to represent my neighbors, but I need your support to keep up this fight.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3863%2E21716%2EURubas)
Hi, it’s Sarah McBride.
I’m the Democratic nominee for Congress in Delaware, and I’m thankful to have your support as I seek a second term.
**But this election is not about me — it’s about whether we’re able to deliver for hardworking Americans who deserve so much more than what Republican politicians are offering.**
It has been an honor of a lifetime to represent my neighbors in Delaware and Washington, and we’ve definitely stayed busy working to pass legislation that works in favor of _all_ hardworking Americans.
More of my bills are bipartisan than any other freshman. We’ve brought home millions of dollars in critical investments to the First State. And we’ve stopped every anti-LGBTQ+ bill from becoming law.
That's what happens when we roll up our sleeves and do the work.
**But with a GOP challenger trying to flip our seat red, and Republicans' massive fundraising advantage over Democrats, I need all the grassroots help I can get to win re-election, so I can keep up our fight.**
[**Will you chip in $10 today to help power my re-election campaign?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1358?c0=mcb-em-20260920-1.iBBAIY&refcode=em20260920-3863&t=2&akid=3863%2E21716%2EURubas)

Hi, it’s
Chris.

We’re facing an onslaught of dark-money spending from Donald Trump’s super

Friend, Recently, when Trump was asked about the risks of artificial intelligence, he dismissed public concerns as a "hoax." His answer to _what guardrails AI needs?_ He wrote that the only guardrail required is a "strong and smart (high IQ!) president." What a moron. I’m looking forward to electing one in 2028. Even AI industry leaders have been calling for real government oversight. And a majority of Trump's own voters said they support AI guardrails in a recent poll. When I was a federal scientist at the U.S. Government Accountability Office, I helped spearhead the first comprehensive governmental report on generative AI, in which we warned members of Congress about the risks of this emerging technology. That was in 2023, and they’ve still not passed meaningful regulation to protect people, jobs, and our national security. We've already seen it with the data centers popping up around our own district, straining water and power with almost no oversight. Congress needs leaders who understand risks, take them seriously, and are committed to finding solutions to protect the public. Patriot, if you’re reading this, you might be the only one who can save my behind. I just got a weekly update from my team that has me sweating bullets. Here’s what we already know: **First: **Trump won Georgia in 2024, making Georgia the most competitive Senate election in the Country. **Second:** Jon Ossoff’s got the full support of the Democrat establishment who want him to WIN this race against me and go on to become president in 2028. **Third:** There’s no length the Democrats won’t go to in order to win the November election. **Here’s what I heard this morning: ** **_If we don’t beat Jon Ossoff this year, and kick him out of the Senate, he WILL be the 2028 candidate representing the Democrat Socialists of America. _**
That means the weight of the world is on our shoulders, _**Peter**_. If we don’t beat Ossoff in November, the next time we’re talking about him, it may be too late, and we’ll be calling ourselves comrades rather than friends. Here's the situation, Peter: NY-17 is one of just three districts that split their ticket in 2024 for Kamala Harris and a Republican member of Congress. This is going to be the most expensive and competitive battleground district in the country. **Donald Trump’s super PAC is spending almost $9 million on ads in this race – more than he is spending on any other House race nationwide.** [If you want to take back the House, I am humbly asking you to make a $10 contribution to my campaign to beat Mike Lawler now. With our final quarterly FEC deadline rapidly approaching, there’s never been a more important moment to donate.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcyAfGXt4NM-NrFmFgQbUn1YtLixS6Q_JRcApTLlIlXH23nQd06r4LBcoNkMt_-V1kzpF02kiZRj-nfuxoQcGfLV4zyTzHN8uD8W9vv6w_mmmyizloL9Y0T9BDTzNJzUt7TWwqAG00RNwI46jIxbb1fKPfurb7cHtNSSQynAYIxe3nEAsGf0hwWfF-qgbO4NnqguQdSkiFNAZwwqYThQxfxPUQXy1_5EvajlNkmEK3BFv4xItR1uKrYgyNaURT7nBUlc3dguqS9cT8oVIzMNVQtX7KLHYXZuAX8-HAZBJxJcqTaR0LrdVbtJP6kVnPyDkFL/4u7/kCsu1KP_SFWSavAxbqpmgQ/h1/h001.QC78IsZzo3VuisKZt9Nt4dc5qy7duAd8gLw_HUXQx2k) | [DONATE »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcyAfGXt4NM-NrFmFgQbUn1YtLixS6Q_JRcApTLlIlXH23nQd06r4LBcoNkMt_-V1kz1HfB_7Q8E4tSwJHgSr2f2dTr4MB-1vlvXExACmAXbkxyAuQbBTPNns1EeUYahXJXcuA3GTtTO8E8BxUhv_y0l62kU90l4q0T_IIVc_UsugvnDl8nfQ7HvYsb8Gq8F3CGeGws_2AJmsZ-jWRjPM4wKV_3H_eKsh7Uc3BZYaZudR2apaEClNOVSmEaT--dpd2FXWCuTJaMzPbZfjHyovRh4S23knXrBFkCamgnb-lb2Cbx2O4kSlmD-cMAjyjRxJKn/4u7/kCsu1KP_SFWSavAxbqpmgQ/h2/h001.TpwYCrWRW5HoOq03BXIPUn9iNZNDtMDaurKvR8exqcw)

Part of the strategy behind Trump’s team dumping such a huge amount of money into this race is they want to make us panic — to think there’s nothing we can do to fight back.
But there are two things that I need you to take away from this news:

James Talarico — the 36-year-old "minister" challenging conservative Ken Paxton — is currently leading by six points. Not in Massachusetts. Not in Vermont. _**In Texas**_. Talarico hasn't called himself a socialist radical. He doesn't have to. His own words do the work for him. ❌ White men are the greatest domestic terrorist threat in this country❌ God is "non-binary"
❌ The Bible is pro-abortion
❌ Christianity is "the most violent religion"
❌ There are six genders, not two That's not a caricature. That's the man in his own words. Strip away the "Christian" branding, and the policy agenda underneath is standard-issue far left: open borders, government-run healthcare, abortion up to birth, gun control, welfare for illegal immigrants, and a war on parental rights in schools.

If either candidate wins in November, they'd be the first Democratic socialists ever elected to the U.S. Senate. And let's be honest. Socialist is their label meant to soften what they truly are **—** Marxists. **This rise of full-blown Communism isn't a fringe problem in blue states. This weekend's fuller data complicates that story in a way worth sitting with carefully — not because the underlying facts of the past three weeks were wrong, but because a broader set of indicators suggests the acute phase of the physical energy crisis may have passed even as its political and humanitarian dimensions have not.
| | Development One — The Physical Chokepoint Data Recovered Sharply
---|---
**Verified fact:** Hormuz throughput rose to roughly 2.8 million barrels a day over six recent days, compared with 700,000 barrels a day in August — a fourfold increase. Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline restoration timeline shortened from five-to-six weeks to a matter of days. Brent crude has now fallen for three consecutive sessions to $102.41. **Our interpretation:** this is a larger and more concrete recovery signal than the market absorbed through the week's more incremental, contested reporting. It does not erase the real disruptions documented earlier — European cargo cancellations, damaged pumping stations, ships transiting dark — but it suggests the trajectory has turned, at least for now.
| | Development Two — A Serious, Formally Documented Allegation Now Sits Alongside the Market Story
---|---
**Verified fact:** a UN fact-finding mission found “reasonable grounds to believe” the United States conducted two strikes — on a school in Minab, with more than 120 children reported killed, and on civilians in Lamerd — that it characterized as indiscriminate and constituting war crimes. The White House rejected the findings in strong terms, and the Pentagon said its own investigation continues. **Our interpretation:** this newsletter's mandate is to track how developments transmit into markets and regimes, not to adjudicate contested legal and factual questions of this gravity. What can be said is that a formal international finding of this severity, regardless of how it is ultimately resolved, is a new and independent variable in the war's political trajectory — one that could affect congressional oversight, allied cooperation, or diplomatic leverage in ways separate from the energy-price story.
| | Development Three — Iran's Internal Position Is Weakening on a Longer Timeline
---|---
**Verified fact:** Iran's rial has fallen 44% against the dollar over six months, food inflation has reached 127.5% year-over-year, crude loadings are down roughly 85%, and the regime held a 330,000-participant Basij mobilization on September 18 while pledging indefinite domestic security deployments. **Our interpretation:** a 10-day pause in Iranian strikes on host states, read against this backdrop, looks less like diplomatic goodwill and more like a regime under severe internal economic and security strain choosing to manage that strain rather than escalate externally. This is a meaningfully different explanation for the recent lull than the more optimistic diplomatic framing markets have periodically priced in.
| | Why This Sits at the Center of the Board
---|---
**Current classification: The energy dimension is moving toward CONFIRMATION of de-escalation; the political and humanitarian dimension has just opened a new, unresolved front; and Iran's internal position points toward continued strain regardless of external military posture.** All three regimes are real and are moving somewhat independently of each other, which is itself the most important finding of this weekend's review: markets, politics, and the war's human cost are no longer telling exactly the same story.
| | What Would Change the Classification
---|---
On energy: whether next week's actual Hormuz shipping data confirms the fourfold volume recovery as durable, or whether it proves to be a temporary window tied to the 10-day pause in strikes. On the UN findings: any further steps in the Pentagon's own investigation, or any concrete diplomatic or congressional response beyond the White House's initial rejection. On Iran: whether the domestic mobilization and economic strain produce any visible change in the regime's external posture once the current pause, for whatever reason it exists, ends.

* * *
This past week marked the beginning of Hispanic Heritage Month and if you have seen any posts about it on social media, you might have seen something along the lines of, "Happy Hispanic Heritage Month except to MAGA Latinos."
This has long been a common sentiment for many Latin Americans and Lefty Latinos since, according to them, any MAGA or Republican Latino is a "race traitor" or has "self-hate." They believe we are betraying our people and want to "white" Americans.
Putting aside some of those declarations incorporate "Latinx" or "Latine" to avoid using "Latino," this common feeling is one that is rife with hypocrisy.
## _WATCH:_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ad648ec2-a3d1-47f3-b3fb-3c6ff2631a4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Latinos in the United States have done a very good job presenting to White Leftists on, "All of us, somos una gran familia, we're all one big, happy family." They might have fooled White liberals, but they can't fool me.
The hypocrisy is that Latinos who are born and raised in the U.S. are expected to have a loyalty to our "motherland" that is not practiced by Latinos in Latin America. Of course, this does not apply to everyone, but there is no denying the bigotry and biases against one each other are very real.
The dirty secret is that the wide range of Latinos and Hispanics are at constant odds with each other when Americans aren't looking. Don't believe me? Watch what happens when you call a Mexican a Guatemalan or when you call a Colombian a Venezuelan and vice versa.

# **Will Trump declare an election emergency before the midterms?**
Kalshi trading markets **[currently show a 14% chance](https://substack.com/redirect/8ec57e85-25a8-4879-8406-81ab53d1f60e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that President Trump declares an election emergency via executive action before the November 4 midterms this year.

* * *
_**(Piece continues)**_
The only reason why they are pushing the "we are unified message" now is because they are the flavor of the month to be used by Democrats to criticize President Donald Trump's immigration policies.
We don't even have to compare different nationalities when talking about this lack of loyalty and solidarity. Using one example, I see all the time on social media how Mexicans from Mexico City look down on Mexicans from el campo, or the countryside in states like Oaxaca and Chiapas. Those states are generally poorer and have a higher indigenous population.
I saw that disdain when I shared a video of indigenous women from the state of Guerrero who pleaded in a video for President Trump to send the U.S. military to take on the cartels who had forced them from their homes.
Of course, Mexicans are more than able to disagree with pleas for help from the United States, but many of these comments went out of their way to denigrate these women for being indigenous, how these types of "uneducated" people are willing to sell out not for money, but tortillas and beans.
This is a big reason why Latinos such as myself prioritize the United States because this is our home and shrug off insults of being "traitors." The loyalty the community loves to profess is conditional and goes away the second you think independently.
At the same time, this does not mean we have self-hate or think we'll be White. We have an appreciation for our heritage, but when it comes to loyalty to country, the United States is number one and I don't think that should be controversial. We have a duty as a citizen, like any other American, to put the needs of our country first.

_Like I said, I’m Joe Males. I’m a Mexican-American who was adopted by two wonderful parents when I was four years old._

**At a young age, I joined the United States Marine Corps to defend our country and ultimately earned the rank of Sergeant before my discharge.** Once I entered civilian life, I started my entrepreneurial career owning a successful small computer business until my son took over the family business.

**Since the Democrats will want to use this to attack me, I will tell you: I was a former Democrat.** I switched over to the Republican Party during the Reagan era once I saw what the Democrats truly stood for. I’ve seen firsthand how today’s Democratic Party has abandoned working families. Every single day, I hear from constituents who are struggling with everyday challenges. I hear them, and I fully agree with them. It’s time for change in California.

**WHY DID I ENTER POLITICS?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=971f4f15bcbe4ce89cd8b0e827a91558&_e=ayb0jdpPBZlmTPjCrBKbq3JWriacw3381JhzauiJK9Sx3pPxw2faRTB6Ef5c-8MDVCzT_0CUDG09RXtd9jxFEzCneb4n3HhF4ESPD1_jgkeN29ZRRRVk_dS3m7_g8oMLVNiRbsdEewxKMDuNtjc_qyqMGnjwTZskmSW2h0Ll6gGxsu8_9KGDi_NmBtOFfXn7SGBvTTtZ4jQQ8o5c1XeTI6PADzmef0bma3bTS_rEDAM_wljvYpVOXXS6EA1nXeoJkeAvPKLFFrYAbunSaRSgnzNCTGQRgatonJSt3pqfH6hobWcqJu3WwJ7Pb4LWeUIkkFI5t8acbhzHAm9RgZGiLfuAKG6_rgzNe7g2WtOua3Msj9iJGlFJkhzIetCqokVKQUYorkS8m2awrizp_PZR6tKyiH7_92KyRY4H357OO0uCObiST_wALAHioi6sxeM53JeQTolIwEYepIBNIHoyu642R1fEahzQ9ZqHm0hu_iWpsdm6UQPvsULACzbkZyPVxuUbuvNGlrqN90XE5dBbdg%3D%3D)

**In short, my son, Nicholas, was tragically stabbed to death and murdered in 2016.**

If you’re a parent, I’m sure you could imagine how devastating this was for me. Nicholas was only 28 at the time and did not deserve what happened.

He had followed in my footsteps and joined the Marine Corps. He was a father to two children – my grandchildren. When it happened, no one came forward with any information, and the case to find the killer went cold.

**I decided to take a stand, to fight for the rule of law and public safety so that no other family has to experience the same tragedy.** Five years later, I ran for City Council in Hemet. I won, and just a few months later, our amazing law enforcement found the killer and arrested him.

**WHAT ARE MY PRIORITIES AS YOUR NEXT CONGRESSMAN?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=971f4f15bcbe4ce89cd8b0e827a91558&_e=ayb0jdpPBZlmTPjCrBKbq3JWriacw3381JhzauiJK9Sx3pPxw2faRTB6Ef5c-8MDVCzT_0CUDG09RXtd9jxFEzCneb4n3HhF4ESPD1_jgkeN29ZRRRVk_dS3m7_g8oMLVNiRbsdEewxKMDuNtjc_qyqMGnjwTZskmSW2h0Ll6gHkZMNcoqQ0BIHQgGTu1mmAptblV3-uSc2WVIHequduekTeOo8F5lrPO75sMKFWccO4VFdN54YLomJfcJ0dP7XFFKNa9jUaSIJwIeG6rwBA4eCR_ExXg5wrYkxDkdS8go9nqRiVOuYBsUeOECp72mHb4IO2Udjreme69Nk74d30TJqY8IXyKDsZmFsopiZHgaLt5CQ7Mkm9R1mIhQBjeRBeAzBTGAQZWY3InMNMj-j-euWQtgqkSiffnAX_UERABTWptQF1ka-oJ2rojFEjC2GpYnx4l41VM5sSeTaZfkpx5Zb6GBjKDGkVkMJEL4vdNP8vce1v5ghPRBuMoxVt6Rl4OxydDNmGyvwCQu5KKt3Pnw%3D%3D)

_**As a former Democrat turned Republican, I know what the Democrat Party is supposed to represent. But ever since the Reagan era, they’ve continued to move farther and farther to the extreme left. Now, they stand for DEI, wokeness, putting Americans last, and doing everything they can to fight against President Trump.**_

**As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration.** America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY.

**Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration.** Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security.

**On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement.** After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness.

**As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around.** Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. I’ll do everything in my power as a Congressman to support our military so we prioritize READINESS over WOKENESS.

**Finally, we must dismantle DEI in every corner of the government.** DOGE’s work to cut wasteful spending has been a great start, but we must continue to fight to lower the cost of living, defend free speech, and usher in the Golden Age of America.

**WHY DO I NEED YOUR HELP?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=971f4f15bcbe4ce89cd8b0e827a91558&_e=ayb0jdpPBZlmTPjCrBKbq3JWriacw3381JhzauiJK9Sx3pPxw2faRTB6Ef5c-8MDVCzT_0CUDG09RXtd9jxFEzCneb4n3HhF4ESPD1_jgkeN29ZRRRVk_dS3m7_g8oMLVNiRbsdEewxKMDuNtjc_qyqMGnjwTZskmSW2h0Ll6gG2sRE4QqEQrd-8WxtbzO1hvVqsZtSnlp7NhLoeAII8YlGdRPSUj93BQ9CEZ-2Wz77NUNbcjW5WFS-4T4_kZsJMqSc1UGa6oXw_tjtA2yT18Quebp_7klVgaLGESwLwBYRz-OjhYv81ZfpDjjgfyv3mgAJrqEowohlqesapk7SaL0iSuSYIVOFnXl2RWENzdtosK7B-eKnX2qijoQyTwJYj1CepYnSrFows41cvLZvmF8sJ1OgH2ZtcmBB8xHpLq2AmbxWZKHBp7OgGn_qG8xyZ0ukwu466iIaABGgdzOj-zf_rcG00-CAUyNpoL6Nzcou8NaH6pfw9hD2d2uQ7Uugb-n83hDWBK7Vlo1_TI_DHKg%3D%3D)

It may seem impossible, but so many Californians are sick and tired of suffering under Gavin Newsom, Nancy Pelosi, and Adam Schiff’s leadership here. I know many people who have left California just because of the politicians who want to turn our beautiful state into a Communist Utopia.

Together, we can fight and WIN._

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

clean_body: This is a longer email, but I’d appreciate it if you took two minutes to read it | Peter, My name is Joe Males, and I’m running for United States Congress in California’s 25th district. WHO AM I? Like I said, I’m Joe Males. I’m a Mexican-American who was adopted by two wonderful parents when I was four years old. At a young age, I joined the United States Marine Corps to defend our country and ultimately earned the rank of Sergeant before my discharge. Once I entered civilian life, I started my entrepreneurial career owning a successful small computer business until my son took over the family business. Since the Democrats will want to use this to attack me, I will tell you: I was a former Democrat. I switched over to the Republican Party during the Reagan era once I saw what the Democrats truly stood for. I’ve seen firsthand how today’s Democratic Party has abandoned working families. Every single day, I hear from constituents who are struggling with everyday challenges. I hear them, and I fully agree with them. It’s time for change in California. WHY DID I ENTER POLITICS? In short, my son, Nicholas, was tragically stabbed to death and murdered in 2016. If you’re a parent, I’m sure you could imagine how devastating this was for me. Nicholas was only 28 at the time and did not deserve what happened. He had followed in my footsteps and joined the Marine Corps. He was a father to two children – my grandchildren. When it happened, no one came forward with any information, and the case to find the killer went cold. I decided to take a stand, to fight for the rule of law and public safety so that no other family has to experience the same tragedy. Five years later, I ran for City Council in Hemet. I won, and just a few months later, our amazing law enforcement found the killer and arrested him. WHAT ARE MY PRIORITIES AS YOUR NEXT CONGRESSMAN? As a former Democrat turned Republican, I know what the Democrat Party is supposed to represent. But ever since the Reagan era, they’ve continued to move farther and farther to the extreme left. Now, they stand for DEI, wokeness, putting Americans last, and doing everything they can to fight against President Trump. As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration. America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY. Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration. Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security. On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement. After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness. As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around. Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. I’ll do everything in my power as a Congressman to support our military so we prioritize READINESS over WOKENESS. Finally, we must dismantle DEI in every corner of the government. DOGE’s work to cut wasteful spending has been a great start, but we must continue to fight to lower the cost of living, defend free speech, and usher in the Golden Age of America. WHY DO I NEED YOUR HELP? Simply put – the Radical Left has a stranglehold on California. Just like they’re trying to flip Texas Blue, I’m trying to flip California Red. It may seem impossible, but so many Californians are sick and tired of suffering under Gavin Newsom, Nancy Pelosi, and Adam Schiff’s leadership here. I know many people who have left California just because of the politicians who want to turn our beautiful state into a Communist Utopia. But Newsom, Pelosi, and Schiff have MILLIONS of dollars in reserve, ready to spend against my campaign to prevent common sense leadership. They only care about lining their own pockets, even if their constituents suffer. It’s going to be an uphill battle, but if there’s one thing I learned as a Marine, it’s that the only way to create a better tomorrow is through dedicated hard work and grit. Together, we can fight and WIN. | Thank you for taking the time to read all of this. I truly appreciate it. Semper Fidelis, Joe Males Meet Joe Males: Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission. Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved. Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same. Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy. During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met. I spent this weekend in Arizona, spent a lot of time in Maricopa County. I did a TV interview, spoke at events, and talked to a lot of people who are working hard to make sure Democrats win up and down the ballot in November.
The interview was for Sunday Square Off on 12News. They asked me why I won't move on from January 6th.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/df4372a0-e9eb-4fea-bbf3-0e7f74c1c5a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Here's what I told them: I can't move on because it's not over.
The people who attacked the Capitol that day. Some of them are running for office right now. Some of them won their primaries. One of them is running for Congress in Rhode Island and calls himself a "proud J6er." That's not the past. That's the ballot.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Iz7wF0Pv3K0wn5WTEEt70036VvKfJdwV4HpR9LmmPss?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=216639375)
Arizona matters for a lot of reasons. Katie Hobbs is a governor who has stood up for voting rights in a state where that fight is real and her opponent? Andy Biggs, was loud in demanding the people who assaulted police on January 6th were released from prison and pardoned. Legislative races on the ballot there could determine whether Arizona looks like a functioning democracy in two years or something else entirely.
I went because I made a promise to myself after January 6th: I'm not going to stay quiet while the people who want to undo democracy run for the offices that control it.
November is six weeks away. If you're in Arizona, vote. If you know someone in Arizona, call them this week. Don't wait.
We held the line that day. We have to hold it again on November 3rd.
-- Harry

I'm blessed to represent and call my friend, an artist named John "Congo Cowboy" Ntibonera. A refugee from war torn Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This is personal. Please share it

---|---|---
Mourners bury victims of the ADF massacre near Komanda, Ituri province (Human Rights Watch, 2025).
On the night of August 28, fighters of the Islamic State Central Africa Province swept into the villages of Mabakoa and Biam in Ituri province, in the northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo. They shot and hacked 29 Christians to death and set roughly forty homes on fire as families fled into the dark. The next day, in the village of Amani, nine more Christians were beheaded and two others killed at the village edge. In one wave of raids, at least 72 Christians were massacred -- that is the count by Barnabas Aid, one of the few organizations still bothering to count. Since mid-July, more than 200 Christians have been killed in Ituri alone.
This is not an anomaly. It is a rhythm. Barnabas Aid puts the toll at more than 1,370 Christians killed in northeastern Congo since December 2024 by the Allied Democratic Forces, the Ugandan-born Islamist militia that pledged allegiance to ISIS and now fights as its Central Africa Province. The pattern is almost liturgical in its repetition. In February 2025, seventy Christians were herded into a church near Lubero, in North Kivu, and beheaded. In July 2025, fighters attacked a night vigil at a Catholic church in Komanda, killing 43 worshippers -- nine of them children, a count confirmed by the UN peacekeeping mission itself. On Maundy Thursday this year, more than 70 villagers were killed overnight in Mambasa territory; Christian monitors counted 43 dead at a single vigil, several of them beheaded with machetes. In May, Radio Okapi reported at least 50 civilians killed in one week. Machetes, night raids, burned homes, abducted children. The weapon is terror, and the churches are chosen targets.
And Ituri's agony is compound. The province is also the epicenter of the country's current Ebola outbreak, layered on top of a war that has already displaced millions across the east. A place that may now be the most dangerous spot on earth in which to kneel and pray is also among the least reported on earth, period.
So let us talk about the arithmetic of silence. What has the world's machinery of conscience produced in response to 1,370 dead? Press releases. Condolence statements that use the word "outrage" the way a bureaucrat uses a rubber stamp. Blue-helmet patrols photographed for institutional archives. There has been no emergency session of the Security Council called because of these massacres. No dedicated commission of inquiry hunting their evidence. No surge of Western correspondents. No hashtags, no landmarks lit, no parliaments debating motions into the night -- save, disgracefully, a lone early day motion in one corner of Westminster.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee767297-79b5-4933-b771-20f0021e82ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In April 2014, Boko Haram kidnapped almost three hundred girls attending school in Chibok, Nigeria. The #BringBackOurGirls campaign emerged as a global activist movement in the aftermath of that kidnapping.
Compare this with the institutional energy the same bodies can summon when they choose. Elsewhere in the world's crises, emergency sessions have been convened within days. Formal genocide determinations have been issued, amplified, and argued across every front page on the planet. Ambassadors have been recalled and sanctions drafted overnight. I do not begrudge any of that -- every people's suffering deserves that machinery, and any honest argument about those cases deserves to be heard. The scandal is that the machinery is switched on and off at will: deployed at full voltage when the accused perpetrator is a state that can be shamed and litigated in the West's courts of opinion, and powered down to a murmur when the killers are an ISIS franchise with machetes and the victims are poor, Black, rural Christians whose governments cannot threaten a veto or move a market.
Be honest about what that pattern means. It means the vocabulary of atrocity is rationed, and the rationing is political. When the dead fit a narrative that flatters or advances the priorities of the powerful, the word "genocide" is deployed with instant fluency. When the dead are villagers of Ituri, the same institutions suddenly discover restraint and reach for "clashes," "instability," "violence in the east" -- euphemisms that would never survive a week if applied to a better-located corpse. To say this is not to attack any faith or any people. The ADF murders Muslims as well; Congolese Muslim leaders have condemned them; the enemy is the militia and its ideology, not a religion. But squeamishness about naming the killers of Christians is not neutrality. Neutrality between the machete and the neck it descends upon is a lie, and silence is its currency.
Let no one mistake this for a competition of suffering. Demanding that Congo's dead be counted diminishes no other victim anywhere; there is no quota on grief, only a hierarchy the powerful have built, and in that hierarchy African Christians rank at the very bottom -- beneath wars with oil leverage, beneath victims who can lobby, beneath atrocities whose perpetrators can be denounced at zero cost to the denouncer's interests. A hundred and seventy journalists can be dispatched to a single foreign trial in Europe; barely a handful are assigned to a province where 200 people have been hacked and burned since July. That is not objectivity. That is the arithmetic of who we have decided matters.
What the world owes Ituri is not complicated. **One** : an emergency briefing at the Security Council and a dedicated international commission of inquiry on the ADF's atrocities, with evidence preserved and handed to the International Criminal Court. **Two** : a protection surge -- reinforced peacekeeping, joint operations with Congolese and regional forces, and actual defenses for the villages that keep being rebuilt and re-burned. **Three** : a humanitarian response equal to the convergence of massacre, Ebola, and displacement now crushing millions. **Four** : accountability -- sanctions on the ADF's financiers and facilitators. **Five** : coverage. Assign a correspondent. Put the words "beheaded in a church" in an algorithm friendly headline and watch the room go quiet.
And what can ordinary people do? Write. Share. Support the organizations still counting the dead -- Barnabas Aid, International Christian Concern, Open Doors. Say the names of the places the wires ignore: Mabakoa. Biam. Amani. Kasanga. Komanda.
The dead of Ituri were farmers and students, infants and elders, congregants gathered for a vigil who expected to walk home at dawn. The world looked away -- not because it could not see, but because they were the wrong dead, in the wrong country, killed by the wrong killers. History will not ask what we said about our principles. It will ask what we saw and chose not to see. "Never again" is either a universal promise or an ornament for the comfortable. The Christians of Ituri are asking which one it is. So should we all.

clean_body: A Reckoning for the World's Conscience | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? A Reckoning for the World's Conscience | | | Sep 20 | | | | | | | | | | | | I'm blessed to represent and call my friend, an artist named John "Congo Cowboy" Ntibonera. A refugee from war torn Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This is personal. Please share it | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Mourners bury victims of the ADF massacre near Komanda, Ituri province (Human Rights Watch, 2025). On the night of August 28, fighters of the Islamic State Central Africa Province swept into the villages of Mabakoa and Biam in Ituri province, in the northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo. They shot and hacked 29 Christians to death and set roughly forty homes on fire as families fled into the dark. The next day, in the village of Amani, nine more Christians were beheaded and two others killed at the village edge. In one wave of raids, at least 72 Christians were massacred -- that is the count by Barnabas Aid, one of the few organizations still bothering to count. Since mid-July, more than 200 Christians have been killed in Ituri alone. This is not an anomaly. It is a rhythm. Barnabas Aid puts the toll at more than 1,370 Christians killed in northeastern Congo since December 2024 by the Allied Democratic Forces, the Ugandan-born Islamist militia that pledged allegiance to ISIS and now fights as its Central Africa Province. The pattern is almost liturgical in its repetition. In February 2025, seventy Christians were herded into a church near Lubero, in North Kivu, and beheaded. In July 2025, fighters attacked a night vigil at a Catholic church in Komanda, killing 43 worshippers -- nine of them children, a count confirmed by the UN peacekeeping mission itself. On Maundy Thursday this year, more than 70 villagers were killed overnight in Mambasa territory; Christian monitors counted 43 dead at a single vigil, several of them beheaded with machetes. In May, Radio Okapi reported at least 50 civilians killed in one week. Machetes, night raids, burned homes, abducted children. The weapon is terror, and the churches are chosen targets. And Ituri's agony is compound. The province is also the epicenter of the country's current Ebola outbreak, layered on top of a war that has already displaced millions across the east. A place that may now be the most dangerous spot on earth in which to kneel and pray is also among the least reported on earth, period. So let us talk about the arithmetic of silence. What has the world's machinery of conscience produced in response to 1,370 dead? Press releases. Condolence statements that use the word "outrage" the way a bureaucrat uses a rubber stamp. Blue-helmet patrols photographed for institutional archives. There has been no emergency session of the Security Council called because of these massacres. No dedicated commission of inquiry hunting their evidence. No surge of Western correspondents. No hashtags, no landmarks lit, no parliaments debating motions into the night -- save, disgracefully, a lone early day motion in one corner of Westminster. | | ---|---|--- In April 2014, Boko Haram kidnapped almost three hundred girls attending school in Chibok, Nigeria. The #BringBackOurGirls campaign emerged as a global activist movement in the aftermath of that kidnapping. Compare this with the institutional energy the same bodies can summon when they choose. Elsewhere in the world's crises, emergency sessions have been convened within days. Formal genocide determinations have been issued, amplified, and argued across every front page on the planet. Ambassadors have been recalled and sanctions drafted overnight. I do not begrudge any of that -- every people's suffering deserves that machinery, and any honest argument about those cases deserves to be heard. The scandal is that the machinery is switched on and off at will: deployed at full voltage when the accused perpetrator is a state that can be shamed and litigated in the West's courts of opinion, and powered down to a murmur when the killers are an ISIS franchise with machetes and the victims are poor, Black, rural Christians whose governments cannot threaten a veto or move a market. Be honest about what that pattern means. It means the vocabulary of atrocity is rationed, and the rationing is political. When the dead fit a narrative that flatters or advances the priorities of the powerful, the word "genocide" is deployed with instant fluency. When the dead are villagers of Ituri, the same institutions suddenly discover restraint and reach for "clashes," "instability," "violence in the east" -- euphemisms that would never survive a week if applied to a better-located corpse. To say this is not to attack any faith or any people. The ADF murders Muslims as well; Congolese Muslim leaders have condemned them; the enemy is the militia and its ideology, not a religion. But squeamishness about naming the killers of Christians is not neutrality. Neutrality between the machete and the neck it descends upon is a lie, and silence is its currency. Let no one mistake this for a competition of suffering. Demanding that Congo's dead be counted diminishes no other victim anywhere; there is no quota on grief, only a hierarchy the powerful have built, and in that hierarchy African Christians rank at the very bottom -- beneath wars with oil leverage, beneath victims who can lobby, beneath atrocities whose perpetrators can be denounced at zero cost to the denouncer's interests. A hundred and seventy journalists can be dispatched to a single foreign trial in Europe; barely a handful are assigned to a province where 200 people have been hacked and burned since July. That is not objectivity. That is the arithmetic of who we have decided matters. What the world owes Ituri is not complicated. One : an emergency briefing at the Security Council and a dedicated international commission of inquiry on the ADF's atrocities, with evidence preserved and handed to the International Criminal Court. Two : a protection surge -- reinforced peacekeeping, joint operations with Congolese and regional forces, and actual defenses for the villages that keep being rebuilt and re-burned. Three : a humanitarian response equal to the convergence of massacre, Ebola, and displacement now crushing millions. Four : accountability -- sanctions on the ADF's financiers and facilitators. Five : coverage. Assign a correspondent. Put the words "beheaded in a church" in an algorithm friendly headline and watch the room go quiet. And what can ordinary people do? Write. Share. Support the organizations still counting the dead -- Barnabas Aid, International Christian Concern, Open Doors. Say the names of the places the wires ignore: Mabakoa. Biam. Amani. Kasanga. Komanda. The dead of Ituri were farmers and students, infants and elders, congregants gathered for a vigil who expected to walk home at dawn. The world looked away -- not because it could not see, but because they were the wrong dead, in the wrong country, killed by the wrong killers. History will not ask what we said about our principles. It will ask what we saw and chose not to see. "Never again" is either a universal promise or an ornament for the comfortable. The Christians of Ituri are asking which one it is. So should we all. | | ---|---|--- \--- Sources: Barnabas Aid (Aug 2026 casualty reports); International Christian Concern (Apr 2026); Radio Okapi/Xinhua (May 2026); BBC and UN MONUSCO (Komanda, July 2025); Open Doors and Aid to the Church in Need (Feb 2025); UNHCR/IOM (displacement and Ebola figures); Human Rights Watch (photography). [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3236%2E251025%2EC_I-Pt ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3236%2E251025%2EC_I-Pt ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter,

Earlier this month, Elon Musk filed with the FEC to spend some of his
nearly $1 trillion in Michigan to help Mike Rogers and stop us from
winning. Musk spent big in 2024, and we saw a red wave put Trump back in
the White House.

We’re already being outspent and out-advertised. I’m worried it could get
worse. And the thing about Elon is he has virtually unlimited money. He
could spend only 0.5% of his net worth, and it would change this whole
race.

But what we showed in the primary, where we were outspent 11-to-1, is that
we can still beat the big money if we put up good enough numbers of our
own.

So, look, I know folks like us can’t donate millions of dollars like they
can. We don’t have to. Because if something like 1-in-4 of the people
reading this email decide, “You know what? I can step up and give
$10,” we will be able to raise enough to counter their
attacks and spread our good word to the voters of Michigan.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260920-3-ak.kXmQkN&amount=10&refcode=em20260920-3236&t=1004&akid=3236%2E251025%2EC_I-Pt ]Peter, can
I count on you to be one of those folks who can donate today? Whether you
can give a lot or a little doesn’t matter. What matters is that enough of
us pitch in.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260920-3-ak.kXmQkN&amount=10&refcode=em20260920-3236&t=1005&akid=3236%2E251025%2EC_I-Pt ]Count me in ››

These mega donors like Elon, they’re not spending against me because they
think our policies are wrong. They’re spending because they think they can
put in a few million dollars and get back a whole lot more in tax breaks.
They’re spending to protect their own pocketbooks.

I'm not telling you this to scare you. We can get outspent and still win.
But we can't get outspent by any number and still win.

If Elon buys every ad break between now and November, most Michiganders
will only ever hear his version of me. They won’t hear our message. And
then it won't matter how good our ideas are, because people won’t be
hearing them at all.

So your donations right now mean absolutely everything.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260920-3-ak.kXmQkN&amount=10&refcode=em20260920-3236&t=1006&akid=3236%2E251025%2EC_I-Pt ]Please, help us counter this Elon influx. Be one of those to give
today.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260920-3-ak.kXmQkN&amount=10&refcode=em20260920-3236&t=1025&akid=3236%2E251025%2EC_I-Pt ]Donate $10 ››

I’m so grateful to this team. You are the reason we have a fighting
chance. Even up against the richest guy on the planet, the president of
the United States, the corporate overlords, and the military-industrial
complex.

Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.

Abdul

body:
They hid the dead and lied about the money. A combat aviator responds. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqGwRYEjOZIY55d82Ij3XqyZ42qxjKJxfrHBH6y-ACd2WcJw7lzglRLoRbA97iqdlGc3LhBAfYR4Y-Af6MJfyihfbKvG-m9cpZKMqWGoxA_QcOl5josaZpRRupvIdNwTp8tQEtudBBcaqLgKZiQXKg8llMSeDu-_gc2V2Z_SCX1G0dyk4qgcXlIiX4FzAZFaolFLIgjjg9LzHkhLCb6nVXGhA/4u7/FQvUYrvzRYiAeaADpBzF0Q/h0/h001.Hm3bV4xFzYKyRAQVD77B6IkNzX7RWKNMmnecTfXng5Y)
---
Peter, Just when you thought the incompetence and infantile machismo of Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump could not get any worse, they delivered a one-two punch of disgrace. This week we learned they did the most dishonorable thing you can do to the men and women who serve. **They hid our war dead.** And they lied about what this war is costing you on top of it.
---
[ **FLIP TX-03 AND END THE DISHONOR** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt81w0VwV7XZ2F_qlIpIjqN82bqHmQkTUYRePpJO6tsHbj2-aUhCt8G0n713YhBiLsQdvnOrflXreqqn8soEerFyPA9nFaNMRC4siVdJ57FRo7_3TdnkmDJM-4N13z_V__S6vdnIXBBT6sHz2OVrtMMbZt9fpeby4f_9yIJPKGpPP0Tv6d8b_20w6D7Qass4OHfJkoUc0h8xs0yvbJTl2uW_K4_6u6usPpSqWt9fTqTYzri6JAsZivIZAdhHUzxbFnpYXhy-oW6RMkYu8Ea_fSWxMsb8DwrdovHGPGTyUMCsp4_0AV2AiOTbqJ5ZAY2-QGYFxibYd9pQgJ8Si9Nf0pUIPoPVlEE16faThpbP-zKc-INlq9Hhj8dlfB-nOQFNarYg/4u7/FQvUYrvzRYiAeaADpBzF0Q/h1/h001.blhvH2dMrwvkde78FdaN0szEvtzYZo8GAJBx0n3D7Mc)
---
The Washington Post revealed that at least 22 American servicemembers have died in this war, while the Pentagon's public count says 18.
Count every American death in the region missing from the public rolls, two more troops who died on other operations and three American contractors supporting our troops, and as many as ten families are grieving somebody this administration never properly acknowledged.
More than 820 of our troops are wounded, many with brain injuries from missiles hitting the bases where they slept.
These liars shuffled our dead into vague database categories, and that paperwork decides what compensation and pension grieving families get.
Cooking the books can shortchange a Gold Star family while Hegseth brags on Fox News about testosterone shots and “warrior ethos”.
I served my country in uniform for 20 years.
We brought our fallen home with honor guards, and we spoke their names, every single one, because that is the last promise a grateful nation keeps.
Watching this administration break that promise sickens me in a way I can’t properly put into words.
[If your blood is boiling like mine, then donate to our campaign to flip TX-03 and send a combat veteran to Congress who will force this Pentagon to answer for every hidden name.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt81w0VwV7XZ2F_qlIpIjqN82hSKml4y5EXl7D5Xc9HBVXjMVNDC7O43zwUiAqC67lLYKAMQApRUG_bdlJWy-MurkbHCLn6WfRuxugRYy4J7eV9rXhZP5LpnWV-QEpJXhW8yOw5h5yxCdLSCFyL0bOXdGnIt7fONECnuHWjwE16ueoIW1TX8agT0tsGstULvkyNmREA6_DwM0WxQ5RrlHlqzJ8yWD8qzNqL1ixGBdbeGMoWDOeAMkJs8iFbk4Z_LtEensBx4gM4qf4wBc8e96z59dI6DpJtoZbJJBoTbEf0sDuB-f4fyBbsOtOpOL4SYjKp7rk5rW-COQULxLTbPeXNvx__3hwQMqGhqo7tcZyqPER9bF62C5hcumuRXfv3i0vXg/4u7/FQvUYrvzRYiAeaADpBzF0Q/h2/h001.Is2thbXCZz5J06ts-x8OxnQEVBUwmaND01_d7Jn4W9s)
Then there is the money.
Central Command's own cost document shows $43.6 billion burned through early September, which works out to roughly $5 billion a month.
That is far beyond anything this administration copped to in front of Congress.
Stop and think about what $5 billion a month could do for this country.
One month of this war could house every homeless veteran in America for a year.
One month roughly matches a full year of federal funding for every community health center in the country.
Instead, that money vaporizes over the Persian Gulf while Trump swears everything is going great.
Like me, Keith Self wore this nation's uniform for decades. But unlike me, Self cheers on these liars at every step and watches them erase our dead without one word of protest.
Peter, I’m mad enough not to mince words here: his silence spits on everyone who has ever served.
[Donate to our grassroots campaign today to help us flip TX-03 and replace a man who forgot what the uniform means with one who never will.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt81w0VwV7XZ2F_qlIpIjqN82X37dhSGePQofi6BG7jPkiDAbOT2ctMjCuTvp5AElRVMpgml4Rc3z6sq3S1Vd74QEmsTwOwt-_I3xNyZFCY2E2OehX9Qn-ZQ4gVYOy6_gOnh_JF6jXeZonhSSgP_VyWH8KsU5e3uNi9mfscKiUCg3DFrDkbzf-bLr79XYB4_cdOZ7Ax_wPvpIfKJ4yR-NdolpPPn3Th8YF9MARHgPAFv9ugGy38GzA_HpmgWtWSLiq0sej-k1bOiTJMtyllNoxFAI3-DqHMJTkkzzmUrv6DKRAOxEjHPpuUXGOoQfFCRBxfmY10lFNEi_CyNKuXqNTSYf6_foQrnolrgiijwLCwLQqha7NffboKxyHtX_xcxN0iQ/4u7/FQvUYrvzRYiAeaADpBzF0Q/h3/h001.32peK7JTNdhjGw9oPtpsMlAI-h3TTV30qNW0YLZ32C8)

clean_body: They hid the dead and lied about the money. A combat aviator responds. | | Peter, Just when you thought the incompetence and infantile machismo of Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump could not get any worse, they delivered a one-two punch of disgrace. This week we learned they did the most dishonorable thing you can do to the men and women who serve. They hid our war dead. And they lied about what this war is costing you on top of it. The Washington Post revealed that at least 22 American servicemembers have died in this war, while the Pentagon's public count says 18. Count every American death in the region missing from the public rolls, two more troops who died on other operations and three American contractors supporting our troops, and as many as ten families are grieving somebody this administration never properly acknowledged. More than 820 of our troops are wounded, many with brain injuries from missiles hitting the bases where they slept. These liars shuffled our dead into vague database categories, and that paperwork decides what compensation and pension grieving families get. Cooking the books can shortchange a Gold Star family while Hegseth brags on Fox News about testosterone shots and “warrior ethos”. I served my country in uniform for 20 years. We brought our fallen home with honor guards, and we spoke their names, every single one, because that is the last promise a grateful nation keeps. Watching this administration break that promise sickens me in a way I can’t properly put into words. Then there is the money. Central Command's own cost document shows $43.6 billion burned through early September, which works out to roughly $5 billion a month. That is far beyond anything this administration copped to in front of Congress. Stop and think about what $5 billion a month could do for this country. One month of this war could house every homeless veteran in America for a year. One month roughly matches a full year of federal funding for every community health center in the country. Instead, that money vaporizes over the Persian Gulf while Trump swears everything is going great. Like me, Keith Self wore this nation's uniform for decades. But unlike me, Self cheers on these liars at every step and watches them erase our dead without one word of protest. Peter, I’m mad enough not to mince words here: his silence spits on everyone who has ever served. If you don't have time to hear my whole pitch, here's my ask: You see, I was once the "acting" president of the United States ‐‐ and while I may have been playing a fictional role, the lessons I learned were very real. I'll let you in on the most important one: Every person has the power to make a difference. You might find that hard to believe right now, after everything we've seen and endured in the past two years. I certainly wouldn't blame you for feeling that way. But look beyond the terrible headlines, and you might just see what I see: Americans of every background and belief, standing up in ways big and small, sacrificing to bring about a future better than our present. Whether they succeed is, in part, up to you. One seemingly small action you can take to help is to join with your fellow Democrats and pitch in $7 to help elect a Democratic Senate majority. Flipping the Senate and bringing accountability to this administration will make a difference, but it will only be possible if we lock hands, raise our voices, and come together ‐‐ that's when we can accomplish truly incredible things. The headwinds we face are strong, but we are stronger. Donald Trump is determined, but we are more determined. And right now, as we stretch our arms toward the future, I hope you'll join me. | | | I introduced a bipartisan bill this week, and the reaction from Trump's own FBI Director tells you everything you need to know about why it's necessary. **The bill is called the No FLOCK Act** , and I introduced it with a Republican colleague, because this shouldn't be a partisan issue. It targets Flock Safety and other automated license plate reader networks that have quietly turned into a nationwide surveillance system. Here's what's actually happening on the ground. A Washington Post investigation found at least 69 police officials who have been accused, charged, or convicted of abusing this technology — using it to track wives, girlfriends, ex-partners, and people they had no legitimate reason to be watching. In Kentucky, one officer used the system more than 2,000 times to stalk his ex-girlfriend. **_And this week, when senators pushed FBI Director Kash Patel on it directly, he didn't express any concern. He defended the technology outright._** Let me be clear about what our bill actually does. It doesn't ban this technology outright, and it doesn't stop legitimate public safety uses like finding stolen cars or locating missing children. What it does is put teeth behind real limits: if a state doesn't restrict license plate readers to a defined set of legitimate uses, it loses some of its federal highway funding. No more unchecked expansion. No more excuses. Because right now, there is functionally no limit on what this data can be used for once it's collected, or who can access it. Local police departments have handed this data to ICE. Officers have used it to stalk people in their personal lives. And Trump's own FBI Director just told Congress, on the record, that he's fine with how it's being used. I am not fine with it. Taxpayers should not be funding the construction of a surveillance state that can be turned against them, their neighbors, or anyone this administration decides to target next. This is exactly why I built Equal Opportunity Now — to support leaders who will stand up for privacy and civil liberties, even when it means taking on their own party's administration to do it. **[Will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us hold the line on this?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139614216/647925312/1090555623?amount=25&refcode=260920_noflockrs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3N2ViMzUxMy00YmI1LWYxMTEtYTZhNy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=soncQ5S9-jiwd1GyhGHRvPzEHBdlUjjHAwnuIRkVnzE=)**

body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/131955?t=6&akid=28993%2E878179%2E8WaHiB) Hi friend, it’s Dr. Annie Andrews.

There’s a lot of new eyes on this campaign, so I wanted to take a second to reintroduce myself.

I’m the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in South Carolina. _But that’s not it._

I’m also a mom of three who does school pick ups and watches Bluey before bed. I’m a pediatrician of twenty years. In other words, I’m not your typical politician.

In fact, this is the last thing I ever thought I’d be doing. But I knew someone had to step up for the people of South Carolina.

**Our campaign is people-powered by grassroots donors like you.** I don't have a network of wealthy donors or billionaire friends. I don't have decades of political favors to call in.

What I do have is twenty years of sitting across from families in some of the scariest moments of their lives, listening to what they actually need, and trying to help.

That's the experience I'm bringing to this race. Not a perfect political resume. A real life, spent in service to the people in this state.

[I’m running for the U.S. Senate to fight for the families, kids, and communities that need someone in their corner. So, if you’re ready to win in November, split a donation between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project today. »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/131955?t=7&akid=28993%2E878179%2E8WaHiB) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Annie Andrews and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/131956?t=8&akid=28993%2E878179%2E8WaHiB)

subject: A new Siena poll just dropped that shows our campaign in the lead for the first time
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
A brand-new poll just showed something that's never happened before.
Friend, look at this:
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260920_1_ak.eqdY1p&refcode=em20260920-926&%3Bamount=5&t=2&akid=926%2E127862%2E7GSQJv)
In his four campaigns for governor, Greg Abbott has _never once_ been shown trailing in a statewide Texas poll. _That just changed._
**_A brand-new poll just showed us ahead of Abbott by four points,_** while he's asking Texans for a fourth term. Not within range. Not closing the gap. Ahead. For the first time.
Here’s what’s happening: Texans are getting a clear look at what twelve years of Greg Abbott has actually cost them. Rising grocery bills. Rising property taxes. Data centers flooding the state while the people footing the bill get nothing back. And when they look at me, they’re seeing someone who’s spent her career fighting for Texas families — not just for the people at the top.
**None of this happens without you.** We are competitive in this race because of the 170,000 people who've chipped in to build this campaign. Our people-powered movement is working. We are clearly breaking through.
But Abbott has a firehose of money aimed at us — $67 million in the bank, and he's already outspent us 10-to-1. He's never had to run from behind before. With this poll out there, he's going to open that firehose all the way to drown out our campaign before Texans vote.
We can't match him dollar for dollar. But we can outnumber him — that's how we got here. 170,000 donors have helped build this campaign into one that can win. I’m asking every one of you to dig a little deeper, right now, to keep us competitive.
**[Can you split $5 right now between Aaron Ford and my campaign to help us keep building a campaign that can defeat Greg Abbott and take Texas back?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260920_1_ak.eqdY1p&amount=5&refcode=em20260920-914&t=3&akid=926%2E127862%2E7GSQJv)**

Greg Abbott has never polled behind in a race for governor. Not once. Now that he has, he's going to come at us with everything he's got. We need everything you've got, too.
Gratefully,
Gina

Data centers flooding the state while the people footing the bill get nothing back. And when they look at me, they’re seeing someone who’s spent her career fighting for Texas families — not just for the people at the top. None of this happens without you. We are competitive in this race because of the 170,000 people who've chipped in to build this campaign. Our people-powered movement is working. We are clearly breaking through. But Abbott has a firehose of money aimed at us — $67 million in the bank, and he's already outspent us 10-to-1. He's never had to run from behind before. With this poll out there, he's going to open that firehose all the way to drown out our campaign before Texans vote. We can't match him dollar for dollar. But we can outnumber him — that's how we got here. 170,000 donors have helped build this campaign into one that can win. I’m asking every one of you to dig a little deeper, right now, to keep us competitive. Greg Abbott has never polled behind in a race for governor. Not once. Now that he has, he's going to come at us with everything he's got. We need everything you've got, too. Gratefully, Gina
